text:
🐱👑 THE BANDIT KING
CHAPTER 14: THE PRICE OF A MIRACLE 🐟🏰

CREATED BY: The Fool (@ChenY60787)
CO-CREATOR: @NearPump 💙
Previously...

A thousand fish fell from the sky.

The Bandit Kingdom celebrated its first great festival.

Merchants prospered. Citizens rejoiced. Travelers spread stories of the little king who had called upon the heavens.

And somewhere in an old book, a forgotten legend known as the Glorious Fish began to stir.

But while His Majesty enjoyed the celebrations...

HIS KINGDOM WAS ABOUT TO FACE A PROBLEM THAT NO AMOUNT OF FISH COULD SOLVE.

🏘️ 1. THE KINGDOM THAT GREW TOO FAST

Three weeks after the Festival of a Thousand Fish, the Bandit Kingdom was almost unrecognizable.

New merchants arrived every morning.

Caravans lined the roads.

Craftsmen built workshops.

Families came searching for work and safer lives.

The former supply station had become a thriving town.

And now...

It was running out of room.

"Chancellor!"

An exhausted clerk rushed into Lucien Vale's office.

"The eastern market is overcrowded!"

Another entered.

"Two merchant caravans are waiting for warehouse space!"

A third shouted:

"Residents are complaining about water shortages!"

Lucien looked up from his desk.

"...Anything else?"

A fourth clerk appeared.

"The royal kitchen is requesting another shipment of dried fish!"

Silence.

Lucien slowly removed his glasses.

"OF COURSE IT IS."

Across the room, His Majesty sat comfortably on a velvet cushion.

"Meow!"

Translation: Excellent news.

💰 2. THE TRUE COST OF PROSPERITY

Lucien summoned the general and the five original adventurers.

A large map covered the table.

Red markers indicated overcrowded districts.

Blue markers represented water sources.

Yellow markers showed proposed construction sites.

Lucien pointed toward the town center.

"Our commercial revenue is increasing."

The general smiled.

"Then the kingdom is prospering!"

"Yes."

Lucien placed another document on the table.

"But prosperity is not the same as stability."

The room grew quiet.

"More residents require more housing."

"More merchants require roads and warehouses."

"More trade requires sanitation, security, and reliable administration."

He paused.

"And all of those things cost money."

One adventurer frowned.

"Can't we simply build more houses?"

"We can. But who owns the land? Who maintains the roads? Who pays for the wells?"

The general studied the map.

"So our greatest weakness is no longer our military strength."

Lucien nodded.

"It's whether our institutions can keep up with our growth."

His Majesty examined the map.

Then placed one tiny paw on a blue marker.

"Meow!"

The general gasped.

"Your Majesty has identified the water supply!"

Lucien stared at the kitten.

"...That's because the marker looks like a fish."

🚰 3. THE WATER DISPUTE

The first serious conflict began in the eastern district.

A group of merchants had financed a private well.

They wanted to charge residents for access.

But nearby families argued that the price was too high.

The dispute quickly attracted a crowd.

"We paid for the construction!"

"And our children need water!"

"Then who pays for maintenance?"

"Why should basic water access depend on how much money we have?"

The general arrived with several guards.

"Everyone, remain calm!"

The crowd quieted.

But the disagreement remained.

One merchant turned toward her.

"General, we're not criminals."

"We invested our own money."

A resident stepped forward.

"And we're not asking for everything to be free."

"We just need a fair arrangement."

The general hesitated.

She could command soldiers.

She could defend roads.

She could defeat bandits.

But this...

WAS NOT A PROBLEM THAT COULD BE SOLVED WITH A SWORD.

⚖️ 4. THE CHANCELLOR'S SOLUTION

Lucien arrived that afternoon.

He listened to both sides.

Then examined the construction records.

"The merchants financed the well."

"Yes."

"The residents require reliable access."

"Yes."

"And neither side wants the well to fall into disrepair."

Both groups nodded.

Lucien adjusted his glasses.

"Then we have a common interest."

He proposed a temporary agreement.

The investors would receive a defined return through regulated fees.

Basic household water access would be protected.

Maintenance costs would be publicly recorded.

And a small committee of merchants, residents, and town officials would oversee the arrangement.

The merchant representative considered the proposal.

"So our investment is protected?"

"Within the agreed limits."

The resident representative asked:

"And the prices cannot suddenly double?"

"Not without a transparent review."

After a long discussion, both sides agreed to a trial period.

The general watched in admiration.

"You resolved the conflict without drawing a sword."

Lucien smiled.

"That's usually preferable."

Then he added:

"Of course, we still need more wells."

🏗️ 5. A CITY NEEDS MORE THAN A KING

That evening, Lucien presented a broader development plan.

New residential districts.

Expanded roads.

Additional warehouses.

Public wells.

Sanitation services.

And a permanent administrative office to coordinate them.

The general studied the proposal.

"An ambitious project."

"A necessary one."

One of the adventurers raised a hand.

"Can the kingdom afford all of this?"

"Not immediately."

Lucien pointed to several marked areas.

"We must prioritize essential infrastructure and build in stages."

Another adventurer asked:

"What about the merchants? Will they help?"

"Some will invest where they expect reasonable returns."

"And the residents?"

"They should have a voice in decisions that affect their neighborhoods."

The general nodded slowly.

"A kingdom is more than its army."

Lucien looked toward the window.

"Much more."

Outside, workers were repairing a road.

Merchants were unloading supplies.

Children were playing near newly built houses.

THE KINGDOM WAS NO LONGER JUST A PLACE PEOPLE PASSED THROUGH.

IT WAS BECOMING A PLACE PEOPLE CALLED HOME.

🐱 6. HIS MAJESTY'S GREAT CONSTRUCTION INSPECTION

The following morning, the general decided that His Majesty should inspect the new construction sites.

The five adventurers accompanied him.

Workers lined up respectfully.

"LONG LIVE THE BANDIT KING!"

The kitten sat in a small royal carriage.

His crown glittered.

His red cape fluttered.

And his attention was focused entirely on a nearby fish vendor.

"Meow!"

The general smiled.

"His Majesty wishes to inspect the market!"

Lucien, who had joined them, sighed.

"Of course he does."

At the construction site, the kitten hopped onto a pile of wooden beams.

A worker gasped.

"His Majesty is examining the materials!"

Another whispered:

"Such dedication!"

Then the kitten spotted a small mouse.

His ears twitched.

His tail rose.

And—

WHOOSH!

He leaped forward.

"YOUR MAJESTY!"

The mouse darted between two stacks of timber.

The kitten chased it.

The workers scrambled to clear the path.

And suddenly...

CRACK!

A rotten wooden support collapsed.

A stack of unused planks fell harmlessly into an empty section of the yard.

Everyone froze.

The foreman rushed over.

"That support was defective!"

He examined the timber.

"If we'd used these materials in the new houses..."

The general stared at the kitten.

"Your Majesty..."

Lucien closed his eyes.

"Don't."

"YOU DISCOVERED A DANGEROUS CONSTRUCTION FLAW!"

"HE WAS CHASING A MOUSE!"

The workers began cheering.

"LONG LIVE THE KING!"

The kitten emerged from behind a barrel.

The mouse had escaped.

"Meow..."

Translation: Mission failed.

📜 7. THE QUESTION OF LAND

Later that week, another problem emerged.

The proposed expansion extended beyond the territory currently administered by the Bandit Kingdom.

Some of the land fell under Lord Blackthorn's jurisdiction.

Other areas were subject to older commercial rights and unresolved claims.

Lucien spread the maps across his desk.

"We cannot simply build wherever we wish."

The general frowned.

"Even if the land is unused?"

"Unused does not mean unclaimed."

He placed a copy of the proposed Northern Open Trade Charter beside the map.

"Our previous negotiations established a possible framework for cooperation."

"But the charter has not yet been finalized."

The general understood.

"Then we must return to the negotiating table."

"Exactly."

One adventurer looked concerned.

"Will Blackthorn agree?"

Lucien considered the question.

"He has reasons to support a stable trading partner."

"But he also has reasons to protect his own authority."

The general folded her arms.

"And Duchess Evelyne?"

"She may offer financing and commercial expertise."

Lucien paused.

"But we must ensure that investment does not become control."

The room fell silent.

For the first time, the kingdom's growth was forcing it to confront the limits of its political independence.

♟️ 8. TWO NEIGHBORS, TWO OPPORTUNITIES

Inside Blackthorn's castle, an adviser presented the latest reports.

"The Bandit Kingdom is seeking land for expansion."

Lord Blackthorn examined the map.

"Naturally."

"My lord, should we reject their request?"

"Why?"

The adviser hesitated.

"They are becoming increasingly influential."

Blackthorn nodded.

"Which makes their stability important."

He pointed toward the northern roads.

"A prosperous trading town benefits our merchants."

"But uncontrolled expansion creates disputes."

He considered the matter.

"Prepare a proposal."

"Defined boundaries. Road access. Security responsibilities. Compensation where appropriate."

The adviser bowed.

"And if they refuse?"

"Then we negotiate."

Blackthorn looked toward the forest.

"A competent ruler does not create enemies without reason."

In the Silverriver Principality, Duchess Evelyne studied the same development reports.

"More residents. More warehouses. More demand for transport..."

Her adviser smiled.

"A promising investment opportunity."

"Indeed."

"Shall we renew our previous offer?"

Evelyne shook her head.

"Not unchanged."

She examined Lucien's earlier proposal.

"The chancellor has already made it clear that his kingdom will not surrender exclusive control of its trade."

"Then what do you suggest?"

"Offer financing for specific projects."

"With clear returns, limited terms, and independent oversight."

Her adviser blinked.

"More modest than our original proposal."

Evelyne smiled.

"A smaller agreement that succeeds can be more valuable than a grand agreement nobody accepts."

🌑 9. THE SHADOWS CHANGE THEIR STRATEGY

Far from the celebrations and negotiations, the mysterious organization gathered in secret.

Their black emblem, crossed by three silver lines, lay upon the table.

An agent delivered his report.

"The kingdom is expanding."

Another added:

"Construction demand is rising."

"Timber. Stone. Transport. Skilled labor."

The commander listened carefully.

"And their greatest weakness?"

The agent opened a ledger.

"They are growing faster than their institutions can manage."

The commander smiled faintly.

"Then perhaps we have been approaching this incorrectly."

An officer frowned.

"Should we attack another caravan?"

"No."

The commander pointed toward the expanding town.

"Destroying trade has only encouraged them to cooperate."

"Then what should we do?"

The commander tapped the ledger.

"Let us see who profits from their growth."

A long silence followed.

"Find the contractors."

"Find the suppliers."

"Find those who believe the kingdom owes them more."

The officer bowed.

"And then?"

The commander leaned back.

"We won't need to break their walls if we can turn their interests against one another."

🌙 10. THE PRICE OF A MIRACLE

Late that night, Lucien stood on the balcony overlooking the town.

The general joined him.

"You're still working?"

"Someone has to."

Below them, lanterns illuminated the new streets.

Workers returned home.

Merchants closed their shops.

Families gathered around dinner tables.

The general smiled.

"It's beautiful."

Lucien nodded.

"It is."

She looked toward him.

"Do you ever regret joining this kingdom?"

He considered the question.

"Sometimes."

The general laughed.

"Because of the fish budget?"

"Mostly."

Then his expression softened.

"But look at them."

He gestured toward the town.

"People came here because they saw an opportunity."

"Now they're building homes, businesses, and relationships."

"They're beginning to depend on one another."

The general looked toward the royal chamber.

"And all because of His Majesty."

Lucien smiled slightly.

"Perhaps he brought us together."

"But keeping this kingdom alive..."

He looked toward the lights.

"THAT IS OUR RESPONSIBILITY."

Inside the royal chamber...

His Majesty was sleeping peacefully.

His crown rested beside his pillow.

His red cape covered his tiny body.

And beneath one paw...

Was a dried fish.

He purred softly.

"Meow..."

Translation: Five more minutes.

He knew nothing of water disputes.

Nothing of land rights.

Nothing of foreign investment.

Nothing of enemies studying the kingdom's growing pains.

But outside his window...

Thousands of people were working to build something that had begun with a ridiculous little robbery in the forest.

A kingdom that existed because people needed it.

A kingdom that grew because people believed in it.

And a kingdom that would survive only if those people learned how to govern it together.

Far away, a messenger rode through the northern night.

In his satchel were two letters.

One bearing the seal of Lord Blackthorn.

The other bearing the crest of Silverriver.

Both were addressed to Chancellor Lucien Vale.

Both concerned the future of the growing kingdom.

And both would require difficult decisions.

THE AGE OF ACCIDENTAL VICTORIES WAS NOT OVER.

BUT THE AGE OF REAL RESPONSIBILITY HAD BEGUN.

🐱👑🐟

TO BE CONTINUED...

text:
🐱👑 THE BANDIT KING
CHAPTER 13: THE FESTIVAL OF A THOUSAND FISH 🐟🎉

CREATED BY: The Fool (@ChenY60787)
CO-CREATOR: @NearPump 💙
Previously...

His Majesty demanded fish.

The heavens answered.

Thousands of fish fell upon the Bandit Kingdom.

The general witnessed a miracle.

The chancellor suffered a financial and administrative nightmare.

And the rest of the world began wondering whether the tiny orange king had somehow earned the favor of heaven.

But the strangest consequence of the fish rain...

WAS STILL TO COME.

🐟 1. THE MORNING AFTER THE MIRACLE

The sun rose over the Bandit Kingdom.

Workers had finally cleared the streets.

The fish that passed inspection had been cleaned, preserved, distributed, or prepared for sale.

And Chancellor Lucien Vale had not slept.

"Three warehouses filled."

"Additional preservation workers hired."

"Emergency sanitation expenses..."

He stared at his ledger.

"...And somehow, the royal fish budget is STILL over its limit."

Across the room, the tiny orange kitten sat on a velvet cushion.

His golden crown tilted slightly.

His red cape was covered in fish crumbs.

"Meow!"

Translation: More fish.

Lucien closed his eyes.

"Your Majesty, I am begging you."

The general entered with a stack of letters.

"Chancellor! Wonderful news!"

Lucien opened one eye.

"...What kind of news?"

"The people wish to celebrate His Majesty's miracle!"

Silence.

"Celebrate?"

"Yes! With a grand festival!"

Lucien looked at the kitten.

The kitten looked at Lucien.

"Meow!"

Translation: A fish festival?!

Lucien whispered:

"PLEASE TELL ME THIS DOESN'T INVOLVE FREE FISH."

🎉 2. A FESTIVAL IS BORN

Within hours, the town square was overflowing with excitement.

Merchants offered to sponsor food stalls.

Fishermen volunteered to demonstrate preservation techniques.

Craftsmen proposed decorations.

Children began drawing pictures of their king surrounded by falling fish.

One elderly merchant stepped forward.

"Your Majesty's kingdom protected our caravans when others would not."

Another nodded.

"And after the terrible attacks, the miracle gave everyone something to celebrate."

A third raised his hand.

"Let us hold a festival to remember this day!"

The crowd cheered.

"THE FESTIVAL OF A THOUSAND FISH!"

The general raised her sword.

"A magnificent tribute to His Majesty!"

Lucien quietly examined the merchants' proposals.

"...Private sponsorship."

"Temporary market permits."

"Additional visitors."

"Potential trade revenue..."

He paused.

Then adjusted his glasses.

"Actually..."

The general smiled.

"You approve?"

Lucien sighed.

"Provided we establish a budget."

The crowd erupted in celebration.

The kitten heard only one word.

"Fish."

His ears stood straight up.

👑 3. THE KING'S FIRST PARADE

The following afternoon, the first Festival of a Thousand Fish began.

Colorful banners hung across the streets.

Children wore tiny paper crowns.

Merchants sold fish-shaped pastries.

Musicians played cheerful songs about the king who had commanded the sky.

And at the center of it all...

A royal carriage rolled through the streets.

Inside sat His Majesty.

The tiny orange kitten.

Wearing his golden crown.

His magnificent red cape.

And an expression of complete confusion.

"Meow?"

Translation: Where are we going?

The five original adventurers walked beside the carriage.

One laughed.

"Remember when he tried to rob us in the forest?"

Another grinned.

"Now he's getting a royal parade!"

A third pointed toward the crowd.

"Look! They're cheering for him!"

The kitten spotted a fish-shaped pastry.

His eyes widened.

"MEOW!"

He leaped from the carriage.

The general screamed.

"YOUR MAJESTY!"

The adventurers rushed after him.

The crowd gasped.

Then someone shouted:

"THE KING HAS DESCENDED TO GREET HIS PEOPLE!"

Thunderous applause followed.

Lucien, watching from the balcony, covered his face.

"...Of course they think that."

🏛️ 4. THE STATUE OF THE KING

At the center of the square stood a magnificent new statue.

A small orange cat.

A golden crown.

A flowing cape.

One paw raised toward the heavens.

Below it, an inscription read:

"THE KING WHO CALLED UPON THE SKY."

The general admired it proudly.

"A fitting monument to His Majesty's greatness."

Lucien examined the construction invoice.

"At least the merchants paid for it."

The five adventurers approached.

One tilted his head.

"Isn't the statue a little too serious?"

Another laughed.

"He looks like he's commanding an army!"

A third shook her head.

"He was literally yelling because he wanted breakfast."

The general folded her arms.

"Great historical moments are not always understood by those who witness them."

Lucien stared at her.

"...You realize you just described the problem perfectly?"

Before she could answer, a commotion erupted.

"YOUR MAJESTY!"

The kitten had climbed onto the statue's pedestal.

Someone had placed dried fish beneath it as an offering.

And His Majesty...

WAS EATING THE OFFERINGS.

The crowd fell silent.

The general stepped forward.

"His Majesty is accepting the people's tribute!"

The adventurers burst into laughter.

Lucien took out his ledger.

"...Do ceremonial offerings count toward the royal fish allowance?"

The kitten hissed.

"MEOW!"

Translation: ABSOLUTELY NOT!

📜 5. THE STORY THAT GREW WINGS

As evening approached, storytellers gathered around the festival fires.

One described the fish rain.

"I saw it myself! His Majesty raised his paws, and the sky answered!"

Another added:

"The clouds parted at his command!"

A third declared:

"Surely such a king has been blessed by fate!"

The stories grew grander with every telling.

By sunset, some claimed the kitten had summoned a thousand fish.

Others insisted it had been ten thousand.

One particularly enthusiastic bard announced:

"A HUNDRED THOUSAND FISH DESCENDED AT THE KING'S COMMAND!"

Lucien nearly dropped his drink.

"THAT IS NOT WHAT HAPPENED!"

The bard bowed.

"Ah, Chancellor! A modest servant of the great king!"

"I AM CORRECTING YOUR NUMBERS!"

But the crowd was already singing.

The little king who raised his paw,

And filled the heavens with silver awe!

No crown too small, no dream too high,

For fish shall fall from the northern sky!

The general wiped away a tear.

"Beautiful."

Lucien stared into the distance.

"I'M LIVING INSIDE A HISTORICAL MISUNDERSTANDING."

🌟 6. THE LEGEND OF THE GLORIOUS FISH

Near the edge of the festival, an elderly traveling storyteller listened to the songs.

He smiled faintly.

"How curious..."

A young merchant turned toward him.

"What is?"

"A king whose destiny is tied to fish."

The merchant laughed.

"That describes His Majesty perfectly!"

The traveler opened an old, weathered book.

"Long ago, there were stories of a treasure known as..."

"THE GLORIOUS FISH."

The merchant leaned closer.

"A treasure?"

"So the old tales say."

"Was it made of gold?"

"Perhaps."

"Was it magical?"

"Some claimed it was."

"Where is it now?"

The old man shook his head.

"No one knows. Some say it was lost with an ancient northern kingdom. Others believe it never existed."

The merchant frowned.

"Then why mention it?"

The storyteller looked toward the festival.

"Because legends have a strange habit of finding new meanings."

He closed the book.

"And sometimes, the people who become part of those legends never know it."

Across the square, the kitten was chasing a fish-shaped lantern.

"MEOWWWW!"

The old storyteller chuckled.

"...Especially that one."

💰 7. THE CHANCELLOR DISCOVERS SOMETHING UNEXPECTED

Late that night, Lucien reviewed the festival accounts.

He expected disaster.

Instead...

"Market revenue increased."

"Temporary lodging fully occupied."

"Merchants funded most of the decorations."

"Food vendors reported record sales."

He checked the figures again.

Then a third time.

"...Interesting."

The general entered.

"How much did the celebration cost us?"

Lucien looked up.

"Less than expected."

"Really?"

"And it generated additional commercial activity."

The general smiled.

"Then His Majesty's wisdom—"

"NO."

She blinked.

"Chancellor?"

"This festival succeeded because merchants, residents, workers, and visitors all found reasons to participate."

He tapped the ledger.

"Nobody ordered them to build these markets."

"Nobody forced them to sponsor the celebration."

"They wanted to."

The general looked toward the glowing square.

"Because they believe in His Majesty."

Lucien considered that.

"...Perhaps."

Then he smiled slightly.

"Or perhaps they've begun to believe in the kingdom they've built together."

For once, the general did not argue.

Outside, the festival bells continued ringing.

♟️ 8. THE WORLD TAKES NOTICE

In Blackthorn's castle, a report arrived.

"The Bandit Kingdom has established an annual festival commemorating the fish rain."

Lord Blackthorn raised an eyebrow.

"An annual festival?"

"Yes, my lord. Merchants are already discussing next year's event."

His adviser frowned.

"Should we be concerned?"

Blackthorn considered the question.

"A festival is not a military threat."

He examined the trade figures.

"But a population developing shared traditions is becoming more than a temporary trading camp."

He set the report down.

"We may soon be negotiating with something that intends to last."

In Silverriver, Duchess Evelyne received a similar report.

"An annual festival. A growing market. Songs about the king..."

She smiled.

"Remarkable."

Her adviser asked:

"Your Grace, do you believe the miracle was genuine?"

Evelyne shook her head.

"That is not the question that interests me."

"Then what is?"

"How does a kingdom become real?"

She looked at the festival illustration.

"Sometimes through conquest."

"Sometimes through treaties."

"And sometimes..."

"Because enough people begin acting as though it already exists."

🌑 9. THE ENEMY'S NEW PROBLEM

In a hidden chamber, the mysterious organization gathered again.

The black emblem with three silver lines rested upon the table.

An agent delivered his report.

"The kingdom's merchants are returning to the eastern roads."

Another added:

"Public confidence has recovered."

A third hesitated.

"And the festival has attracted new traders."

The commander remained silent.

Their attacks had been intended to weaken trust.

Instead, the kingdom had found something new to unite around.

"Then the next operation must be different."

An agent bowed.

"Shall we attack the festival next year?"

"No."

The commander looked at the map.

"An attack might only strengthen their legend."

He pointed toward the growing town.

"First, we must understand what holds this kingdom together."

The chamber fell silent.

Far away, festival bells echoed across the northern roads.

🐱 10. THE KING'S GREATEST ACHIEVEMENT

Midnight arrived.

The festival was ending.

Lanterns floated above the town square.

Merchants packed away their stalls.

Children fell asleep wearing paper crowns.

The five adventurers sat beneath the new statue.

And in the middle of their little group...

His Majesty was sleeping.

Curled into a tiny orange ball.

His crown had slipped over one ear.

His red cape covered his paws.

A half-eaten dried fish rested beside him.

One adventurer smiled.

"He's exhausted."

Another laughed.

"He spent the whole day chasing food."

The general approached quietly.

"Today, His Majesty gave the people something precious."

Lucien stood beside her.

"A reason to celebrate together."

The general nodded.

"A shared memory."

Lucien looked at the sleeping kitten.

"...And perhaps the beginning of a tradition."

For a moment, nobody spoke.

They simply watched their little king sleep.

Then the kitten opened one eye.

"Meow?"

Translation: Is there more fish?

The adventurers burst into laughter.

Lucien sighed.

The general smiled.

And the little king went back to sleep.

Far beyond the town, an old traveler walked beneath the stars.

Inside his bag rested a weathered book.

Its faded cover bore the image of a golden fish.

He paused upon a distant hill and looked back at the festival lights.

"The Glorious Fish..."

He smiled.

"Perhaps that old story will be told again."

Then he continued down the road.

And in the kingdom behind him...

A new tradition had been born.

Not through conquest.

Not through prophecy.

Not through the will of a mighty ruler.

But because thousands of ordinary people had found something worth celebrating together.

AND THEIR KING STILL ONLY WANTED FISH. 🐱👑🐟

TO BE CONTINUED... 🌙

The festival has ended.

The kingdom has gained a tradition.

Its enemies are reconsidering their plans.

And somewhere in the north, an ancient legend is waiting to be rediscovered...

WHAT IS THE GLORIOUS FISH? 🌟🐟

text:
PRAYER OF RESTORATION, HOPE, AND A NEW NIGERIA
24 October 2026 | 4AM

Fabulous Father,

At this hour, while Nigeria sleeps, we bring this nation before You.

1. RESTORATION
Restore this land, 
O Lord.

Where there has been blood on the soil, let there be harvest again.

Where there has been fear on our roads, in our farms, and in our homes, let there be safety.

Where our children have left because hope left first, bring hope home.

2. SAFETY
Secure this nation.

Secure our streets, 
our markets, our schools, our churches and mosques.

Secure the farmer in Benue, the trader in Onitsha, the fisherman in Bayelsa, the driver in Lagos, the student in Zaria or Kano or Ibadan.

Let a man go out to work in the morning and return in peace in the evening.

3. PROSPERITY
Prosper the work of our hands, this day always. 

You said our labour 
shall not be in vain. 

Today we ask that You break the cycle where we work so hard and have so little to show.

Let our labour bring more than enough food.

Let the ground 
yield again.

Let factories work again.

Let salaries be enough to live, not just to survive.

Let our barns be full.

4. DIGNITY
Take away this struggle to make ends meet that has become the daily prayer of every household.

Replace hustling with harvest. Replace struggle with surplus.

Give us a Nigeria where a young man does not need to steal to eat.

Where a young woman does not need to sell her dignity to pay rent.

Where a father can feed his family and still hold his head high.

5. REAL HOPE
Replace the false hope that keeps us poor — the one Brother Jero sells — with real hope.

Real hope that work is rewarded.

Real hope that honesty pays.

Real hope that tomorrow can be better than today.

Let Nigeria live again.

Let Nigeria 
feed herself again.

Let Nigeria work again.

6. FOR JANUARY 2027
And as we prepare for the elections in January 2027 — _date to be confirmed with INEC_ —

Give us sense, Lord. 
Give us wisdom.

For those of us who will be offered money by politicians, let us know in our hearts that it is okay to collect our share of the national cake that was already taken from us, and still go into that booth and vote our conscience.

Let no 5k, no 10k, no 50k, no bag of rice buy our future.
If they bring money, let us take it as small restitution — but let our thumb still be free. Let our vote still be ours.

Deliver us from the poverty that makes us sell our voice for one night and suffer for four years.

Let us not sell Nigeria again, Lord. Not this time.

We speak over Nigeria: Restoration of safety. Restoration of abundance. Restoration of dignity in labour. Restoration of power in the vote.

In the name of the One who gives us power to get wealth,

Amen. Amen. And Amen.

text:
MY PUBLIC ENDORSEMENT: JIM RUTLEDGE FOR MARYLAND ATTORNEY GENERAL

Race-baiting has failed our communities. Fearmongering has failed our communities. Excessive divisive messaging has failed our communities. And political loyalty must never take precedence over public integrity and accountability.

The recent announcement concerning Republican Jim Rutledge’s proposal for an independent Maryland Bureau of Investigation resonates with me on a deeply personal and professional level.

Having spent more than 25 years in federal law enforcement, I understand the importance of independent investigations, prosecutorial integrity, and holding individuals accountable regardless of their political connections, financial influence, or positions of authority.

And having personally experienced the frustrations of navigating our legal system, these issues are more than political talking points to me.

Public corruption, white-collar crime, financial exploitation, and the misuse of public resources deserve serious attention throughout Maryland, particularly here in Prince George’s County.

For far too long, in my opinion, our political conversations have been dominated by partisan loyalties, familiar endorsements, emotional manipulation, and divisive rhetoric.

Every election cycle, we see many of the same political figures and organizations promoting familiar messages. But I believe we should be asking much more important questions:

Where is the accountability? Where is the independent oversight? Who is investigating allegations of public corruption? Who is protecting taxpayers? And what measurable improvements are our communities experiencing?

Political affiliation should never determine who gets investigated, who gets prosecuted, or who receives protection under the law.

I have long challenged the dominance of one-party politics in Prince George’s County. However, I also recognize that corruption is not exclusive to Democrats, Republicans, or independents. Misconduct must be investigated wherever credible evidence leads.

That is precisely why I believe Maryland’s Attorney General must exercise independent judgment, free from improper partisan influence.

I am particularly interested in Rutledge’s proposal to establish an independent investigative bureau to examine public corruption, taxpayer fraud, and organized crime.

Of course, any such proposal deserves careful examination, including how the agency would be established, funded, supervised, and protected from political interference.

But the underlying principle is one I strongly support: No elected official, political appointee, government employee, or politically connected individual should be above the law.

I also believe our younger generations offer hope for the future. As more residents challenge traditional political narratives and demand transparency, I hope we will see a stronger culture of independent thinking and accountability.

We cannot continue allowing race, political labels, personalities, and fear to dominate every important public policy discussion.

Our communities deserve more.

For these reasons, I am publicly endorsing Republican Jim Rutledge for Maryland Attorney General.

My endorsement does not mean I am becoming a Republican. It does not mean I am aligning myself with a political party.

I remain an independent, unaffiliated candidate and an independent thinker.

I have no political handlers, no obligation to defend any party’s agenda, and no interest in allowing political labels to dictate my judgment.

This endorsement reflects my personal assessment of the issues, my professional experience, and my conviction that Maryland would benefit from meaningful debate about independent investigative oversight.

I respect the right of every Marylander to reach their own conclusions and make their own electoral decisions.

We must move beyond personalities and examine policies. Beyond political loyalty and demand accountability.

text:
In 2021 Kevin Spacey was ordered to pay House of Cards' producer $31 million.
With interest it grew to $36 million. The producer cut it to $1 million.
The price: help them prove to their insurer that he had been too sick to work.
In March 2026 a jury decided he hadn't been.

Piers Morgan Uncensored, June 2024.

Morgan asked where he lives now. His Baltimore house was being foreclosed.

"Because I can't pay the bills that I owe."

Was he facing bankruptcy?

"There have been a couple of times when I thought I was going to file, but we managed to sort of dodge it, at least as of today."

The video below is the rest of that answer.

"How much money do you have?"

"None."

"I still owe a lot of legal bills that I have not been able to pay."

"Many millions. The house itself is many millions."

October 2017. The first allegation goes public.

MRC, the show's producer, suspends him. Netflix cuts ties. The final season is rewritten without him and cut from 13 episodes to 8.

An arbitrator finds he broke MRC's harassment policy with five crew members. $29.5 million in damages, plus costs.

He fights it. In 2022 a Los Angeles judge says it is not even a close case.

He doesn't pay. Interest adds $5 million.

18 December 2023. MRC makes him an offer.

Pay $1 million instead of $36 million. In installments of 10% of his after-tax income.

In return: his medical records, exams by doctors from both sides, and his testimony.

MRC wanted the $29.5 million back from its insurer. The policy covered an actor too sick to work.

After the allegations, Spacey had checked into an Arizona clinic that treats sex addiction.

March 2026. Santa Monica. Five weeks of trial.

Spacey takes the stand. He reads the diagnosis from his discharge papers: sexually compulsive behavior.

He says he doesn't believe it was correct.

The jury rules that his illness was not the main reason he left the show. The insurer owes nothing.

The $29.5 million stays with MRC.

In 2022 a New York jury found him not liable. In 2023 a London jury acquitted him on all nine charges.

In the same Morgan interview he said he had been "too handsy."

"Touching someone sexually in a way that I didn't know at the time that they didn't want."

Morgan asked what he would do now. He raised his fists.

"Get back on the horse."

Four months later he posted a photo from a film set. He was sitting on a horse.

Who should pay the $29.5 million?

text:
🇺🇸 🧠 🚀 If Einstein Were Alive Today, He Would Choose California and Elon Musk to Push the Boundaries of Physics

The idea that Albert Einstein, if he were still alive, would opt for Canadian citizenship rather than remain American overlooks both his historical path and the reality of where the frontiers of science are being advanced today.

Einstein did not choose the United States by default. Fleeing Nazi Germany in 1933, he settled in Princeton, New Jersey, at the Institute for Advanced Study. He filed his first citizenship papers in 1936 and took the oath in October 1940. The judge who naturalized him remarked that his presence constituted “a gain for America.” Einstein even renounced his Swiss citizenship. He remained American until his death in 1955, despite the criticisms he voiced about certain aspects of American society. That choice was not abstract: he preferred a country that offered him the freedom to think, publish, and work without ideological constraint.

Today, the center of gravity for research applied to fundamental physics and breakthrough technologies is in California. That is where the resources, talent, and ambition to push the limits of what is technically possible are concentrated. Elon Musk leads a group of companies there whose projects directly engage questions of physics: propulsion, energy, materials, brain-machine interfaces, and large-scale computing. SpaceX has demonstrated launcher reusability on a scale never before achieved, turning the equations of orbital mechanics and atmospheric reentry into industrial realities. Tesla is advancing energy storage and advanced materials. Neuralink is conducting clinical trials on neural interfaces that link the physics of electrical signals to cognition. These efforts do more than improve existing products; they test limits that public research alone struggles to cross at the same pace.

A contemporary Einstein, trained in relativity and quantum mechanics, would find in this California ecosystem collaborators, data, and infrastructure capable of applying his insights to concrete problems: space propulsion, fusion, or human-machine interfaces. California also offers an environment where ideas can be tested quickly, funded by private capital, and corrected by experience, rather than filtered through slower administrative processes. Einstein always favored freedom of inquiry over institutional comfort. It is hard to imagine him leaving the country that welcomed him in 1933 for a setting where breakthrough innovation remains more dispersed and less ambitious in the domains he would have wanted to explore.

The speculation that the American political climate would drive him toward Canada ignores the criterion that guided Einstein in 1940: the ability to continue his work without obstruction. That criterion would lead him today to remain American, settle in California, and contribute, alongside Elon Musk and his teams, to concretely advancing physics and applied science.

Let me analyze this parlay 🤑🏆

1. LSU moneyline (-237)
LSU at Auburn · 12:00 PM ET
Advantages ✅
The odds imply roughly a 70.3% chance of winning, before sportsbook margin.
LSU only needs to win; there is no point-spread requirement.
Risks ⚠️
Auburn has home-field advantage.
Rivalry games can be unpredictable, especially if LSU struggles with turnovers or protection.
Verdict: A reasonable favorite, but not a guaranteed win.
2. Indiana moneyline (-252)
Indiana at Michigan · 12:00 PM ET
Advantages ✅
The price implies about a 71.6% win probability before margin.
A moneyline is safer than needing Indiana to win by a specific number of points.
Risks ⚠️
Playing at Michigan can be difficult.
If Michigan controls the line of scrimmage or wins the turnover battle, Indiana could lose outright.
Verdict: One of the more attractive legs by odds, but verify the matchup and current team news before relying on it.
3. Tennessee moneyline (+115)
Tennessee at South Carolina · 3:30 PM ET
Advantages ✅
The plus-money price offers a larger return if Tennessee wins.
Tennessee may have the offensive firepower to win a close game.
Risks ⚠️
The odds imply only about a 46.5% chance of winning before margin.
Tennessee is playing away, and South Carolina can make this difficult if it disrupts the offense.
Verdict: A high-risk leg. This is the first pick I would reconsider if you want to make the parlay safer.
4. USC moneyline (-138)
USC at Wisconsin · 7:30 PM ET
Advantages ✅
The odds imply roughly a 58.0% win probability before margin.
USC needs only a win, even if the game is close.
Risks ⚠️
This is a relatively short favorite, so the market sees a competitive matchup.
Wisconsin at home could make the game physical and keep the score close.
Verdict: A plausible pick, but not strong enough to treat as a safe leg.
5. Utah moneyline (-222)
Houston at Utah · 10:15 PM ET
Advantages ✅
The odds imply roughly a 68.3% chance of winning before margin.
Utah has home-field advantage.
Risks ⚠️
Houston could exploit defensive mistakes or keep the game close.
Late games can still produce unexpected results; a favorite's price does not remove upset risk.
Verdict: Reasonable on the odds alone, but check the latest injury reports and matchup information.

text:
Every Sunday evening before dark, my dad hooked an old steel bed frame behind his riding mower and dragged our gravel driveway smooth.

He always turned the mower around twenty feet before our mailbox, leaving the last stretch untouched and covered in weeds.

When I turned sixteen and got my license, I offered to rake the rough gravel by the road to help him out.

He caught my wrist with an iron grip, knocked the rake out of my hand, and looked straight down the empty country road.

"You never smooth the gravel where they step," he said in a whisper. "You let me see their tracks first."

**The Last Twenty Feet**

He let go right away and said sorry, which Dad almost never does. Then he picked the rake up off the ground and hung it back in the shed, and neither of us said anything else about it.

I'd grown up thinking the weedy strip was just Dad being lazy about the end of the driveway. He wasn't a lazy man in any other way. The rest of our place was mowed to the inch.

I wanted to know who "they" were. I thought about it all week. I decided it was something to do with the bank, or a guy Dad owed money to, or maybe the county. Our road is a dead end in Knox County, Ohio, and people don't walk it unless they're lost.

The next Sunday I did what I'd never bothered to do before. After supper I stood at my bedroom window and watched him.

He dragged the driveway like always, put the mower in the shed, and walked down toward the mailbox with his hands in his back pockets. He stopped at the edge of the weeds. Then he crouched, very slowly, for a long time. He looked at the dirt the way you'd read something. After a minute he stood up, nodded once at nobody, and came back in.

When he'd gone to the barn I went down there myself...

text:
Chennakeshava Temple, Belur, Karnataka📍🇮🇳

A Timeless Masterpiece of India’s Glorious Heritage

The magnificent Chennakeshava Temple in Belur, Hassan District, Karnataka, stands as an enduring symbol of India’s spiritual grandeur, architectural sophistication, and extraordinary artistic legacy. A jewel of Hoysala architecture, this sacred monument reflects the remarkable vision, devotion, and craftsmanship that flourished in medieval India.

Commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana in 1117 CE, the temple is celebrated for its exquisite soapstone carvings, intricately sculpted pillars, elaborate ornamental details, and breathtaking sculptural compositions. Every surface reveals the exceptional skill of its artisans, transforming stone into a magnificent expression of faith, imagination, and artistic excellence.

The temple’s exterior walls feature meticulously carved horizontal friezes depicting elephants, lions, horses, and an array of decorative motifs. These intricate sculptural bands enrich the monument’s visual splendour while reflecting the sophisticated artistic traditions and symbolic language of the Hoysala period.

Beyond its architectural magnificence, the temple represents a profound cultural and spiritual legacy, preserving centuries of religious devotion, historical memory, and indigenous craftsmanship. Its enduring beauty offers a remarkable glimpse into the artistic achievements and cultural richness of India’s medieval civilisation.

In 2023, the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, recognising their outstanding universal value. The Chennakeshava Temple at Belur is one of the three monuments included in this prestigious designation, alongside the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu and the Keshava Temple at Somanathapura.

The Chennakeshava Temple is far more than an architectural marvel; it is a testament to India’s timeless heritage, spiritual depth, and exceptional artistic ingenuity. Its magnificent sculptures, intricate craftsmanship, and enduring splendour continue to inspire admiration across generations, securing its place among the treasured monuments of world heritage.

Every carving tells a story, and every stone preserves a legacy. Which aspect of India’s ancient craftsmanship inspires you the most?

" The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat -

In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 1, verses 26-38 (KJV), the angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a young virgin betrothed to Joseph of the house of David in Nazareth. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee, the angel declares. He announces that she will conceive and bear a son, Jesus, who shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest. Mary, troubled yet reverent, asks how this can be since she knows not a man. Gabriel explains the Holy Spirit will come upon her; for with God nothing shall be impossible.

Mary's response is one of the most profound moments in Scripture the only recorded instance where she speaks words of total surrender: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word (Luke 1:38). This Latin phrase, Fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum (Let it be done to me according to your word), is universally known as Mary's Fiat. In that single sentence she offers her entire being body, will, and future to Gods plan of salvation. The angel then departs, and the Incarnation begins.This humble virgin from an obscure village becomes the mother of the Messiah. She travels to visit her cousin Elizabeth (pregnant with John the Baptist), where she sings the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), a soaring hymn of praise that magnifies the Lord for lifting up the lowly.

She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem, wraps Him in swaddling clothes, and lays Him in a manger. She ponders the shepherds and Magis words in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). At the Presentation in the Temple, Simeon foretells a sword will pierce her soul (Luke 2:35). She is present at the wedding in Cana, prompting Jesus first miracle (John 2:1-11), and stands at the foot of the cross, where the dying Savior entrusts her to the beloved disciple (John 19:25-27).

After the Ascension, she is seen praying with the apostles in the upper room, awaiting the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:14).Scripture portrays Mary not as a distant saint but as a real woman of extraordinary faith, courage, and obedience. Though the Bible does not record many of her words, her fiat echoes through salvation history as the perfect model of human cooperation with divine grace. She exemplifies what it means to say yes to God when the cost is everything.Your striking black-and-white artwork beautifully captures this very moment: Mary veiled, head bowed, hands clasped in prayerful surrender, her flowing hair and garments stirred by the unseen wind of the Spirit.

The dramatic lighting and ethereal atmosphere evoke the solemn hush of the Annunciation the instant heaven touched earth through a virgins willing heart. It is a powerful visual meditation on Luke 1:38, inviting viewers to contemplate the same radical trust Mary offered.

$META: The reaction has been much weaker. After the sharp post-earnings drop, the $638–643 zone is worth watching. A move back above $663 would be an early sign of recovery, while a break below support could mean more downside pressure.

𝐕𝐞𝐧𝐨𝐦  more  lethal  than  intended  coated  the  tongue  with  reckless  abandon.  A  𝒘𝒂𝒔𝒕𝒆  …  a  deliberate  definement  that  resounded  with  a  bitter  edge.  Each  syllable  frigid  and  finite  in  protestation  to  the  memories  which  continued  to  plague  the  𝓡𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐨  𝓓𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐧.  A  reluctance  to  simply  𝑙𝑒𝑡  𝑔𝑜,  to  be  rid  of  past  burdens  attested  otherwise.  For  something  of  little  value  could  not  possibly  carry  such  immeasurable  weight.  Yet  he  refused  to  exercise  restraint,  to  revoke  the  damage  done.  Near  a  century  of  mixed  signals  and  tangled  frequencies  —  an  𝐄𝐍𝐃  to  uncertainty.

Sever  the  ties,  carve  out  what  resembled  any  sense  of  𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐲.  Whatever  means  to  relinquish  these  emotions  wavering  his  sense  of  control  would  be  worth  it  …  𝑤𝑜𝑢𝑙𝑑  𝑖𝑡  𝑛𝑜𝑡.ᐣ

     ﹝𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑐  𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑒𝑟𝑒𝑛𝑐𝑒﹞

𝑼𝒏𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒂𝒏𝒕,  a  quality  mutually  shared.  Egos  smothering  any  sense  of  reason  —  one  unable  to  see  the  fault  in  his  desire,  the  other  incapable  of  entertaining  the  concept  of  vulnerability.  𝐅𝐎𝐑𝐆𝐈𝐕𝐄𝐍𝐄𝐒𝐒  never  in  the  cards,  entirely  removed  from  a  deck  shuffled  beyond  and  semblance  of  order.  What  remained  between  the  two  overlords,  a  muddied,  𝑢𝑔𝑙𝑦  thing.  Hours  whiled  away  in  bars,  blood  spilled  in  the  streets  side  by  side  …  quiet  moments  in  companionable  silence.  𝑁𝑜𝑤.ᐣ  Murky,  distorted  and  painfully  distant.

     …  𝑼𝒔.ᐣ

Word  like  a  physical  blow,  blunt  trauma  to  the  shield  of  bravado.  Smile  tensed,  a  subtle  𝑓𝑙𝑖𝑛𝑐ℎ  at  the  term.  Two  letters  bearing  incalculable  weight  and  terrifying  implications.  Reflex  begged  𝐫𝐞𝐯𝐮𝐥𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧  at  the  thought  of  someone  beyond  simply  himself,  selfish  to  a  fault.  And  𝑦𝑒𝑡  …  𝐔𝐬.  A  glimmer  of  something  𝒎𝒐𝒓𝒆,  something  𝓐𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫  dared  not  consider.  Merely  a  figment  of  what  could  have  been,  honeycoated.  Curiosity  be  damned,  he  would  not  falter.  There  were  no  friends  in  𝓗𝐞𝐥𝐥.  No  𝐓𝐑𝐔𝐒𝐓.  No  weakness  permitted.  Only  ambition,  only  power,  𝑜𝑛𝑙𝑦  𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑜𝑙.  Nearly  a  century’s  endeavor  would  not  be  cast  aside  on  sentimentality.

Magic  sparked,  fresh  bolts  fueled  by  unbridled  𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞  beckoned  forth  by  the  media  overlord  which  the  stag  drank  in.  Volatile  and  𝐕𝐈𝐎𝐋𝐄𝐍𝐓  —  emotions  he  could  navigate,  manipulate.  Anger,  a  far  simpler  beast  to  confront  than  sincerity;  blood  and  broken  bones  a  language  𝓐𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫  could  comprehend.  Drown  in  fury,  let  resentment  burn  them  both  from  the  inside  out  to  leave  little  more  than  ash.  𝐷𝑒𝑠𝑝𝑖𝑠𝑒  me,  reject  me,  ℎ𝑎𝑡𝑒  𝑚𝑒.  𝐇𝐚𝐭𝐞  𝐦𝐞.  𝑯𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒎𝒆𝒉𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒎𝒆—

     …  𝑀𝑎𝑘𝑒  𝑡ℎ𝑖𝑠  𝑒𝑎𝑠𝑖𝑒𝑟  𝑜𝑛  𝑢𝑠  𝑏𝑜𝑡ℎ.

Silence  fell  without  preamble,  ire  guttering  out  like  the  wasted  remains  of  a  candle  burnt  at  both  ends.  Once  a  composer  of  𝐐𝐔𝐈𝐄𝐓,  now  uncomfortable  in  what  settled  between.  Crimson-tipped  digits  curled,  nearly  rescinding  the  offer.  A  deal  he  presumed  𝓥𝐨𝐱  would  jump  at  the  chance,  liberty  from  whatever  festered  in  wake  of  the  two  overlords.  Cerise  hues  downcast  in  turn,  mind  mulling  upon  the  proffered  arrangement.  Was  this  not  what  they  𝑏𝑜𝑡ℎ  desired.ᐣ  A  mutual  severance  to  this  lingering  attachment  which  brought  little  more  than  ﹝𝑎𝑔𝑜𝑛𝑦﹞  𝐚𝐠𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐯𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.ᐣ  Perhaps,  reconsideration—

Clipped  gait  an  abrupt  interruption  to  such  𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐬  musings,  cerulean  talons  ensnaring  —    further  nails  in  the  coffin.  And  for  a  𝒔𝒊𝒏𝒈𝒖𝒍𝒂𝒓  𝒎𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕,  the  𝓡𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐨  𝓓𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐧  froze.  Gaze  blown  wide  in  what  only  could  be  perceived  as  shock,  still  and  silent  upon  their  intertwined  hands.  Smile  alarmingly  small.

     𝑂ℎ.  𝐼  𝑠𝑒𝑒.

Perfectly  clear,  disillusioned  —  𝑡𝑒𝑛𝑑𝑒𝑟  fantasies  and  𝐟𝐨𝐧𝐝  memories  swept  away  in  an  instant.  𝑂𝑓  𝑐𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑠𝑒,  naturally  this  would  be  the  progression.  A  deal  was  made  and  𝓥𝐨𝐱,  ever  the  businessman,  accepted  what  was  offered.  All  according  to  plan,  𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐥𝐲  as  intended.  So  𝑤ℎ𝑦.ᐣ  Why  did  the  strongest  sinner  in  𝓗𝐞𝐥𝐥  feel  utterly  𝐇𝐎𝐋𝐋𝐎𝐖.ᐣ  Entirely  void  of  the  triumph,  the  𝑟𝑒𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑓  he  had  anticipated.ᐣ  Numb,  steps  stumbling  in  wake  of  𝓥𝐨𝐱’𝐬  unrelenting  grip  leaving  hardly  a  breath  between.  Screen  near-blinding  at  such  proximity,  his  own  visage  reflected  against  pristine  glass.  𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧  did  not  suit  the  𝓡𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐨  𝓓𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐧.  Had  a  small,  undefinable  part  of  him  𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑙𝑦  longed  for  another  outcome.ᐣ

     ❝ 𝐴ℎ𝑎  …  𝑨𝒉𝒂  𝒉𝒂  𝒉𝒂  … ❞

Laughter  spilled  forth,  unbidden  behind  clenched  fangs.  Features  𝑡𝑤𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑒𝑑,  shock  withering  away  beneath  that  rhythmic  red  glow.  𝐍𝐨.  This  was  a  fitting  end  set  in  motion  decades  ago,  perhaps  more.  The  𝓥𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐭  he  once  knew,  little  more  than  a  dream  smothered  by  the  𝐃𝐄𝐌𝐎𝐍  before  him  now.  And  could  the  same  not  be  said  of  himself.ᐣ  Had  he  not  gouged  out  every  soft  point  buried  within,  nothing  left  but  jagged  edges  and  a  𝐬𝐚𝐯𝐚𝐠𝐞  smile.ᐣ

     ﹝𝑙𝑎𝑢𝑔ℎ  𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑐𝑘,  𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛﹞

     𝐴𝑙𝑙  𝑎𝑠  𝑖𝑡  𝑠ℎ𝑜𝑢𝑙𝑑  𝑏𝑒.  𝑇ℎ𝑖𝑠  𝑖𝑠  …  𝑔𝑜𝑜𝑑.  𝑇ℎ𝑖𝑠  𝑖𝑠  𝒓𝒊𝒈𝒉𝒕.

Shadows  writhed  beneath,  𝐟𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐥  and  unfettered  to  lap  at  their  master’s  heels.  Shade,  entirely  unnatural,  befell  the  two  sinners  invoked  in  the  wake  of  the  deal.  Static  screeched,  frequencies  clashing  as  darkness  consumed  the  radio  overlord.  Features  masked  in  impenetrable  blackness,  save  for  the  virid  glow  of  eyes  and  teeth  contorted  by  𝑔𝑙𝑒𝑒𝑓𝑢𝑙  malice.  Antlers  extended,  branching  outward  like  carnivorous  vines.  Verdant  flames  licked  about  the  two,  symbols  glinting  in  the  flickering  light.  Not  simply  a  display  of  𝐩𝐨𝐰𝐞𝐫,  but  a  𝒔𝒆𝒂𝒍.  A  confirmation  of  their  bargain.

     ❝ 𝑴𝒂𝒓𝒗𝒆𝒍𝒐𝒖𝒔.  I  𝑑𝑜  look  forward  to  featuring  you  on  a  future  broadcast.  𝑻𝒓𝒚  not  to  disappoint  me  now,  𝓥𝐨𝐱! ❞

Words  swept  away,  lost  to  umbral  tides  as  the  demon  decomposed  within  the  very  darkness  he  controlled.  Inky  tendrils  left  to  trail  from  cyan  claws  before  dissipating  in  the  open  air.  Laughter  fizzled  out  in  the  overlord’s  wake.  All  which  lingered  below,  a  single  𝐬𝐡𝐚𝐝𝐨𝐰  —  figured  hunched,  trembling  with  a  seemingly  𝑑𝑒𝑣𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑑  smile.  A  slow  shake  of  its  head  and  it  was  𝐆𝐎𝐍𝐄.

text:
If you can smell your neighbour's smoke, you are breathing their air.

A story from the US this week: a resident said marijuana smoke from the flat next door kept entering her apartment, despite a no-smoking lease. The report doesn't identify the route the smoke took. But an architect can tell you the routes a building offers - and this sketch illustrates one way it can happen.

In a shared-exhaust configuration, flats connect to one ventilation shaft. Air is meant to leave the building through it. But air follows pressure, not intention. Wind, the stack effect in a tall shaft and exhaust fans create pressure differences that can push one flat's air into the shaft - and back out into another home.

Researchers have measured smoke constituents inside homes where nobody smoked (Kraev and colleagues, Tobacco Control, 2009). And smoke is not the only passenger. Investigating a COVID-19 cluster in a Seoul apartment block, Hwang and colleagues found cases along two vertical stacks of flats sharing a bathroom air duct - a possible route for aerosol spread between homes (International Journal of Infectious Diseases, 2021).

A Georgia woman said her next-door neighbour's marijuana smoke kept entering her apartment despite a no-smoking lease - The Times of India https://t.co/nZQmF8S6rb

Now hold two health needs in one frame. Let's assume the neighbour was using prescribed cannabis for a genuine medical need. The resident next door reported that the smoke affected her breathing and her health - and she spent nearly two years asking her building to act before turning to the courts. One person's treatment should not become another person's unwanted exposure.

Goodwill alone cannot control where air travels. Architecture shapes whether those health needs collide: sealed boundaries between flats, properly designed exhaust routes, controlled pressure and suitable filtration can reduce unintended transfer. They do not replace preventing smoke at its source.

That is how health gets affected by architecture. A wall may separate two homes on a floor plan. The design also needs to consider what passes between them in the air.

5,000 YEARS OF BLACK HISTORY: BLACK  STORIES MUST NEVER DIE ✊🏿

The slave trade lasted for centuries. Colonisation followed. 
But the struggle of African people did not end with slavery.

For about 400 years, millions of Africans were taken from their homeland and forced into slavery across North America, South America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Europe and other parts of the world.

When slavery ended, many Africans on the continent faced another brutal reality: colonisation.

Today, descendants of enslaved Africans across the world continue to search for their roots. They preserve their traditions, tell their stories and fight to keep their ancestors' memories alive.

But how much do blacks truly know about one another?

Many in Africa know how Patrice Lumumba was killed and how Thomas Sankara was assassinated in 1987. Yet, how many know the story of Anthony Crawford, a prosperous Black farmer who was lynched in South Carolina in 1916 after disputing the price offered for his cotton? His family was subsequently driven out of town.

His story is one of many painful chapters in Black history.

Black  stories are connected, even when their experiences and the ways they remember them differ.

It is time for Black people across Africa, North America, South America, Latin America and the Caribbean to reconnect, share their histories and learn from one another.

Because pride begins with knowledge. And unity grows when they understand their  shared past.

 This is why a team has launched a crypto project, an initiative bringing 5,000 years of Black history to the blockchain.

Their mission is to preserve history, create educational resources and help ensure that future generations can discover the stories that shaped their people.

Blockchain is their chosen tool for building a lasting, accessible historical record. But technology alone is not enough. They  need research, education, communities and people committed to keeping these stories alive.

Historical sites across Africa and the Americas must be more than tourist attractions. They must be places of learning, remembrance and reflection.

Their children deserve to know what happened. They deserve the truth, the courage of their ancestors and the achievements that history has too often overlooked.

They cannot turn the page of a book they  have not read in full.

They  must remember, educate and preserve—not to promote hatred, but to build understanding, dignity and a better future.

So that it never happens again.

This crypto project is 
5,000 years of Black history. Preserved for generations to come.

Help keep back history alive.

text:
On the Eternity of Hell: Twenty-first Sunday After Pentecost by St. Alphonsus de Liguori.
.
"And his Lord, being angry, delivered him to the torture
until he paid all the debt."--MATT, xviii. 34.
.
In this day's gospel we find that a certain servant, having badly administered the affairs of his master, was found to owe him a debt of ten thousand talents. The master demanded payment; but the servant falling down said: "Have patience and I will pay thee all." The master took pity on him, and forgave the entire debt. One of his fellow-servants who owed him a hundred pence, besought him to have patience, and promised to pay him the last farthing; but the wicked servant cast him into prison. Hearing of this act of cruelty to his fellow-servant, the master sent for him, and said to him: "Wicked servant, I have forgiven thee ten thousand talents, and for a debt of a hundred pence thou hast refused to show compassion to thy fellow-servant. He then delivered him to the tortures till he paid all the debt. Behold, dearly beloved brethren, in these last words, a description of the sentence of the eternal death which is prepared for sinners. By dying in sin, they die debtors to God for all their iniquities; and being unable to make any satisfaction in the other life for their past sins, they remain for ever debtors to the divine justice, and must suffer for eternity in hell. Of this miserable eternity I will speak today: listen to me with attention.
.
1. The thought of eternity is a great thought: so it was called by St. Augustine: Magna cogitatio. According to the holy doctor, God has made us Christians, and instructed us in the maxims of faith, that we may think of eternity. "We are Christians that we may always think of the world to come." This thought has driven from the world so many of the nobles of the earth, has made them renounce all their riches, and shut themselves up in the cloister, there to live in poverty and penance. This thought has sent so many young men into caves and deserts, and has animated so many martyrs to embrace torments and death, in order to save their souls for eternity. "For," exclaims St. Paul, "we have not here a lasting city, but we seek one that is to come." (Heb. xiii. 14.) This earth, dearly beloved Christians, is not our country; it is for us a place of passage, through which we must soon pass to the house of eternity. "Man shall go into the house of his eternity." (Eccl. xii. 5.) In this eternity the house of the just, which is a palace of delights, is very different from the house of sinners, which is a dungeon of torments. Into one of these two houses each of us must certainly go. "In hanc vel illam aeternitatem," says St. Ambrose, "cadam necesse est." (S. Amb., in Ps. cxviii.) "Into this or that eternity I must fall."
.
2. And where the soul shall first go, there she shall remain for ever. "If the tree fall to the south or to the north, in what place soever it shall fall there shall it lie." (Eccl. xi. 3.) On what side does a tree fall when it is cut down? It falls on the side to which it inclines. On what side, brethren, will you fall, when death shall cut down the tree of your life? You will fall on the side to which you incline. If you shall be found inclining to the south that is, in favour with God you shall be for ever happy; but if you shall fall to the north, you must be for ever miserable. There is no middle place: you must be for ever happy in heaven, or overwhelmed with despair in hell. We must all die, says St. Bernard or some other author (de Quat. Noviss.), but we know not which of the two eternities shall be our lot after death. "Necessi morem, post haec autem dubia aeternitatis."
.
3. This uncertainty about his lot for eternity was the constant subject of the thoughts of David: it deprived his eyes of sleep, and kept him always in terror. "My eyes prevented the watches: I was troubled, and I spoke not: I thought upon the days of old, and I had in my mind the eternal years." (Ps. Ixxvi. 5, 6.) What, says St. Cyprian, has encouraged the saints to lead a life, which, on account of their continual austerities, was an uninterrupted martyrdom? It was, he answers, the thought of eternity that inspired them with courage to submit to such unceasing rigours. A certain monk shut himself in a cave, and did nothing else than constantly exclaim: "eternity! eternity!" The famous sinner converted by the Abbot Paphnutius, kept eternity always before her eyes, and was accustomed to say: "Who can assure me of a happy eternity, and that I will not fall into a miserable eternity." The same uncertainty kept St. Andrew Avellino in continual terrors and tears till his last breath. Hence he used to ask every one he met, "What do you say? shall I be saved or damned for eternity?"
.
4. O! that we, too, had eternity always before our eyes! We certainly should not be so much attached to the world. "Quisquis in aeternitatis disiderio figitur, nec prosperitate attollitur, nec adversitate quassatur: et dum nihil habet in mundo quod appetat, nihil est quod de mundo pertimescat." He who fixes his thoughts on eternity, is not elated by prosperity nor dejected by adversity; because, having nothing to desire in this world, he has nothing to fear: he desires only a happy eternity, and fears only a miserable eternity. A certain lady, who was greatly attached to the world, went one day to confession to Father M. D' Avila. He bid her go home, and reflect on these two words always and never. She obeyed, took away her affections from the world, and consecrated them to God. St. Augustine says that the man who thinks on eternity, and is not converted to God, either has no faith, or has lot his reason.
.
"O aeternitas! qui te cogitat, nec poenitet, aut certo fidem non habet, aut si habet, cor non habet." (In soliloq.) O eternity! he who thinks on thee, and does not repent, has certainly no faith, or has lost his heart. Hence St. Chrysostom relates, that the pagans upbraided the Christians with being liars or fools: liars, if they said they believed what they did not believe; fools, if they believed in eternity and committed sin. "Exprobabant gentiles aut mendaces, aut stultos esse Christianos; mendaces si non crederent quod credere dicebant; stultos si credebant et peccabant."
.
5. Woe to sinners, says St. Cesarius of Arles; they enter into eternity without having known it; but their woes shall be doubled when they shall have entered into eternity, and shall never be able to leave." Vae peccatoribus, incognitam ingrediuntur." To those who enter hell, the door opens for their admission, but never opens for their departure. " I have the keys of death and of hell." (Apoc. i. 18.) God himself keeps the keys of hell, to show us that whosoever enters has no hope of ever escaping from it. St. John Chrysostom writes, that the condemnation of the reprobate is engraved on the pillar of eternity, so that it never shall be revoked. In hell there is no calendar; there the years are not counted. St. Antonine says, that if a damned soul heard that she was to be released from hell after so many millions of years as there are drops of water in the sea, or grains of sand in the earth, she would feel a greater joy than a criminal condemned to death would experience at hearing that he was reprieved, and was to be made the monarch of the whole world! But, no! as many millions of years shall pass away as there are drops of water in the ocean, or grains of dust in the earth, and the hell of the damned shall be at its commencement. All these millions of years shall be multiplied an infinite number of times, and hell will begin again. But of what use is it, says St. Hilary, to count years in eternity? Where you expect the end, there it commences. "Ubi putas finem invenire, ibi incipit." And St. Augustine says, "that things which have an end cannot be compared with eternity." (In Ps. xxxvi.) Each of the damned would be content to make this compact with God--Lord, increase my torments as much as thou pleasest; assign a term for them as distant as thou pleasest; provided thou fix a time at which they shall cease, I am satisfied. But, no! this time shall never arrive. "My end," the damned shall say, "is perished." (Lamen. iii. 18.) Then, is there no end to the torments of the damned? No! the trumpet of divine justice sounds in the caverns of hell, and continually reminds the reprobate that their hell shall be eternal, and shall never have an end.
.
6. If hell were not eternal, it would not be so frightful a chastisement. Thomas a Kempis says, that "everything which passes with time is trifling and short." Any pain which has an end is not very appalling. The man who labours under an imposthume or a cancer, must submit to the knife or the cautery: the pain is severe; but because it is soon over it can be borne. But a tooth-ache which lasts for three months without interruption is insupportable. Were a person obliged to lie in the same posture for six months on a soft bed, or even to hear the same music, or the same comedy, night and day for one year, he would fall into melancholy and despondency. Poor blind sinners! When threatened with hell they say: "If I go there I must have patience."
.
But they shall not say so when they will have entered that region of woes, where they must suffer, not by listening to the same music or the same comedy, nor by lying in the same posture, or by tooth-ache, but by enduring all torments and all evils. "I will heap evils upon them." (Deut. xxxiii. 23.) And all these torments shall never end.
.
7. They shall never end, and shall never be diminished in the smallest degree. The damned must for ever suffer the same fire, the same privation of God, the same sadness, the same despair. Yes, says St. Cyprian, in eternity there is no change, because the decree is immutable. This thought shall immensely increase their sufferings, by making them feel beforehand, and at each moment, all that they shall have to suffer for eternity. In this description of the happiness of the saints, and the misery of the reprobate, the Prophet Daniel says: "They shall wake some unto life everlasting, and some unto reproach to see it always." (Dan. xii. 2.) They shall always see their unhappy eternity. Ut videant semper. Thus eternity tortures each of the damned not only by his present pains, but with all his future sufferings, which are eternal.
.
8. These are not opinions controverted among theologians; they are dogmas of faith clearly revealed in the sacred Scriptures. "Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire." (Matt. xxv. 41.) Some will say: The fire, but not the punishment of the damned is everlasting. Such the language of the incredulous, but it is folly. For what other purpose would God make this fire eternal, than to chastise the reprobate, who are immortal? But, to take away every shadow of doubt, the Scriptures, in many other places, say, that not only the fire, but the punishment, of the damned is eternal. "And these" says Jesus Christ, "shall go into everlasting punishment." (Matt. xxv. 46.) Again we read in St. Mark, "Where the worm dieth not, and the fire is not extinguished." (ix. 43.) St. John says: " And the smoke of their torments shall ascend up forever and ever." (Apoc. xvi. 11.) "Who," says St. Paul, "shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction." (2 Thess. i. 9.)
.
9. Another infidel will ask: How can God justly punish with eternal torments a sin that lasts but a moment? I answer, that the grievousness of a crime is measured not by its duration, but by the enormity of its malice. The malice of mortal sin is, as St. Thomas says, infinite. (1, 2, q. 87, art. 4.) Hence, the damned deserve infinite punishment; and, because a creature is not capable of suffering pains infinite in point of intensity, God, as the holy doctor says, renders the punishment of the damned infinite in extension by making it eternal. Moreover, it is just, that as long as the sinner remains in his sin, the punishment which he deserves should continue. And, therefore, as the virtue of the saints is rewarded in Heaven, because it lasts for ever, so also the guilt of the damned in Hell, because it is everlasting, shall be chastised with everlasting torments. "Quia non recipit causae remedium," says Eusebius Emissenus, "carebit fine supplicium." The cause of their perverse will continues: therefore, their chastisement will never have an end. The damned are so obstinate in their sins, that even if God offered pardon, their hatred for Him would make them refuse it.
The Prophet Jeremias, speaking in the name of the reprobate, says: Why is my sorrow become perpetual and my wound desperate, so as to refuse to be healed?" (Jer. xv. 18.) My wound, they say, is incurable, because I do not wish it to be healed. Now, how can God heal the wound of their perverse will, when they would refuse the remedy, were it offered to them? Hence, the punishment of the reprobate is called a sword, a vengeance which is irrevocable. "I, the Lord, have drawn my sword out of its sheath, not to be turned back." (Ezech. xxi. 5.)
.
10. Death, which is so terrible in this life, is desired in hell by the damned; but they never shall find it. "And in these days men shall seek death, and shall not find it: and they shall desire to die, and death shall fly from them." (Apoc. xi. 6.) They would wish, as a remedy for their eternal ruin, to be exterminated and destroyed. But "there is no poison of destruction in them." (Wis. i. 14.) If a man, condemned to die, be not deprived of life by the first stroke of the axe, his torture moves the people to pity. Miserable damned souls! They live in continual death in the midst of the pains of hell: death excites in them all the agony of death, but does not give them a remedy by taking away life. "Prima mors," says St. Augustine, "animam nolentem pellit de corpore, secunda mors nolentem tenet in corpore." The first death expels from the body the soul of a sinner who is unwilling to die: but the second death that is, eternal death retains in the body a soul that wishes to die. "They are laid in hell like sheep; death shall feed upon them." (Ps. xlviii. 15.) In feeding, sheep eat the blades of grass, but leave the root untouched; hence the grass dies not, but grows up again. It is thus that death treats the damned; it torments them with pain, but spares their life, which may be called the root of suffering.
.
11. But, if these miserable souls have no chance of release from hell, perhaps they can at least deceive or flatter themselves with the hope, that God may one day be moved to pity, and free them from their torments? No: in hell there is no delusion, no flattery, no perhaps; the damned are as certain as they are of God's existence that their hell shall have no end. "Thou thoughtest unjustly that I shall be like to thee; but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face." (Ps. xlix. 21.) They shall for ever see before their eyes their sins and the sentence of their eternal condemnation." And I will set before thy face."
.
12. Let us conclude. Thus, most beloved brethren, the affair of our eternal salvation should be the sole object of all our concerns. "The business for which we struggle" says St. Eucharius, "is eternity." There is question of eternity: there is question whether we will be saved, and be forever happy in a city of delights, or be damned, and confined for eternity in a pit of fire. This is not an affair of little importance; it is of the utmost and of eternal importance to us. When Thomas More was condemned to death by Henry the Eighth, his wife Louisa went to him for the purpose of tempting him to obey the royal command. Tell me, Lousia, replied the holy man, how many years can I, who am now so old, expect to live? You might, said she, live for twenty years. O foolish woman! he exclaimed, do you want me to condemn my soul to an eternity of torments for twenty years of life?
.
13. O God! Christians believe in the existence of hell, and commit sin! Dearly beloved brethren, let not us also be fools, like so many who are now weeping in hell. Miserable beings! What benefit do they now derive from all the pleasures which they enjoyed in this life? Speaking of the rich and of the poor, St. John Chrysostom said: "unhappy felicity, which has drawn the rich into eternal infelicity! O happy infelicity, which has brought the poor to the felicity of eternity!" The saints have buried themselves alive in this life, that after death they may not find themselves buried in hell for all eternity. If eternity were a doubtful matter, we ought even then make every effort in our power to escape an eternity of torments; but no, it is not a matter of doubt; it is a truth of faith, that after this life each of us must go into eternity, to be forever in glory or forever in despair. St. Teresa says, that it is through a want of faith that so many Christians are lost. As often as we say the words of the Creed, life everlasting, let us enliven our faith, and remember that there is another life, which never ends; and let us adopt all the means necessary to secure a happy eternity. Let us do all, and give up all; if necessary, let us leave the world, in order to secure eternal happiness. When eternity is at stake no security can be too great. "Nulla nimia securitas," says St. Bernard, "ubi periclitatur aeternitas."

text:
Weekend check

Spot Bitcoin ETFs lose $635.6M in a single session, BlackRock moves big BTC and ETH stacks to exchanges, and $111 oil pushes bitcoin:native toward $81K support.

🔸 ETF flows flip sharply: U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of -$635.6M in one day. BlackRock’s IBIT alone lost -$254M, wiping out the gains from the previous three sessions.
🔹 BlackRock sends hundreds of millions to exchanges: On-chain data shows wallets linked to BlackRock moved 3,215 BTC (~$262.4M) and 38,882 ETH (~$93.2M) to Coinbase Prime. That’s fueling worries about a rebalance or an upcoming sell-off.
🔸 Bull Flag still holds: Even with bitcoin:native pulling back to $81,000–$81,500, the daily Bull Flag pattern is still intact. The longer-term target for a rebound remains $96,000–$97,000.
🔹 Oil and U.S. stocks weigh on the market: Geopolitical tensions have kept Brent crude around $111–$112/bbl, stoking inflation fears. The Nasdaq-100 fell 5.5%, and crypto miners like CIFR, RIOT and MARA dropped 7–8%.
🔸 Record monthly outflows for Ether ETFs: Spot Ether ETFs have shed $1.08B in October, the biggest monthly drain of 2026 so far. That’s keeping ethereum:native stuck around $2,380–$2,410.
🔹 All eyes on the Fed (Oct 27–28): FedWatch puts the odds of the Fed holding rates at 91.7%. That expectation is giving sentiment some footing and helping keep money parked near support.
🔸 Whales buy while retail panics: The number of wallets holding 10–10,000 BTC hit an all-time high of 20,338, after they scooped up another 85,000 BTC during the dips. Meanwhile, retail investors are dumping in a panic.
🔹 Grayscale and the altcoin ETF wave: Grayscale has filed to convert its Bitcoin Cash Trust (BCHG) and Litecoin Trust into exchange-listed ETFs. At the same time, Wall Street is widening access to Uniswap ($UNI) and BCH funds.
🔸 Solana rolls out Alpenglow: Solana has activated its Alpenglow upgrade on mainnet to speed up transaction validation. Still, $SOL slipped with the broader market to $103.
🔹 Ethereum eyes 4-minute finality: Ethereum developers have published a draft settlement design to bring finality down to 4 minutes, which would make DeFi more competitive.
🔸 https://t.co/BY6Jsb5smM launches options trading: The platform now offers Options (Calls & Puts) on BTC, ETH, SOL, AVAX and XRP, settled directly in USDC.
🔹 13-year-old Bitcoin wallets wake up: On-chain trackers spotted some Bitcoin wallets dormant for 13 years moving millions of dollars’ worth of BTC to exchanges in the last 24 hours.
🔸 Derivatives cool off, sentiment neutral: Derivatives volume dropped sharply as Wall Street desks closed for the weekend. Leverage has reset to balanced levels, putting the Fear & Greed Index at 48–50 (Neutral).
