text:
Russian-Indian BrahMos missile is getting future-ready
The arms maker is working furiously to build new variants and up-arm existing ones for future battlefields
Published 24 Oct, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/y6t1rl1Lh8
The BrahMos corporation is working to add more destructive power and reach to its namesake supersonic cruise missile, following its spectacular combat successes last year.
The operational and functional parameters of the missile are being upgraded, and new versions are in the works, the CEO and managing director of the joint venture between India and Russia, Jaiteerth Joshi, told local media recently.
Named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers, the BrahMos is engineered for high-precision, long-range strikes. The missile offers militaries the versatility to engage threats using land, sea, and underwater platforms.
BrahMos earned its stripes last year when the Indian and Pakistani militaries briefly clashed with missiles and drones, following a terrorist attack on civilians in India’s Jammu and Kashmir state.
As the two militaries tested each other with drones, India fired BrahMos missiles to strike hardened high-value targets, including hangars reportedly housing Pakistan’s US-made F-16 fighter jets.
India has said there was not a single interception of the BrahMos during the clashes, dubbed Operation Sindoor, and buyer interest has risen since.
BrahMos Aerospace is a joint venture between India’s DRDO and Russia’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya.
BrahMos’ trajectory into the future
BrahMos started as a land-launched cruise missile, but its developers have worked to give it more flexibility and lethality as battlefield needs evolved and expanded.
The missile, which flies at nearly three times the speed of sound and carries a 200 to 300 kg warhead, had an initial range of 290 km but continuous upgrades have extended its reach.
In 2023, the Indian Air Force (IAF) successfully tested a version with a 450 km range. Mated to the Su-30MKI fighter, this variant, called the BrahMos-A, offers the IAF a standoff precision strike capability that few air forces in the world can match.
There is also a Block III land-attack variant, which can fly very low and approach targets from unexpected angles – dodging any defenses the enemy may try to throw at it.
The BrahMos corporation is working on a long and ambitious list of upgrades. At the top of the current development efforts sits a lighter, air-launched variant.
Christened the BrahMos-NG, it can be flown on the IAF’s other fighter jets, including the domestically produced Tejas light combat aircraft. The Su-30MKI will be able to sortie armed with three of these missiles.
The BrahMos-NG will feature higher domestically-produced content and advanced materials. The Indo-Russian joint venture expects to unveil this prototype by 2027-28.
The BrahMos corporation is also working on a very long-range missile. This version would be able to strike targets up to 1,500 km away, far more than the 290 km range of the original missile unveiled in the early 2000s.
This long-range version is at the conceptual stage, and the company is discussing further upgrades with its Russian joint venture partner. Joshi has told Indian media outlets in recent interviews that the range-extension program will proceed in phases, with test firings from land, sea, and air to validate the missile’s operational capabilities.
Also, on the missile maker’s drawing board is a hypersonic version – the new frontier of modern warfare – currently called BrahMos II.
The concept aims to integrate advanced technologies, state-of-the-art design, and smart materials to field a hypersonic futuristic weapon that will dominate fast-evolving battlefield technology.
BrahMos II will have an “air-breathing” scramjet engine that would boost it to a top speed of Mach 5.

text:
On the false claims by X MAGA NAZI trolls claiming Ukraine is itself responsible for interruptions to satellite network.
.
This is the evidence offered with sources, unlike the disinformation of the X MAGA NAZIs.
.
We know Ukraine already had Starshield access through Pentagon contracts, and we now have confirmation from Ukraine that service at more than 400 km/h is functioning again.
.
There is an important public-policy question: Why was essential communications service for a country defending itself against invasion interrupted without advance warning, and who possessed the authority to make that decision?
.
(The strongest sources for investigating that question further are the October 23 Reuters investigation and October 24 Reuters restoration report.)
.
Ukrainian reporting confirms that Ukrainian drones use Starlink Mini terminals. Reuters and CBS additionally confirm that Ukrainian drones carry receivers operating under Starshield military services.
.
Important new development: Ukraine reports service restored today
October 24 update
Reuters, October 24, 2026:
.
Ukraine’s defense minister, Yevhenii Khmara, announced today that Starlink and Starshield connections are again operating on equipment moving faster than 400 km/h (249 mph).
.
He reported:
“We are recording a speed of over 400 kph. The connection is stable.”
.
Reuters emphasizes that Ukraine has not disclosed the system’s maximum operating speed or confirmed that every capability has been fully restored. Nevertheless, this is a significant improvement over the conditions reported yesterday. (Reuters)
.
This development also strengthens an important conclusion: the approximately 160 km/h restriction was not an inherent technical limit of the equipment used by Ukrainian forces. The service could operate at much higher speeds when permitted to do so.
.
This is particularly important to your question because it establishes that the physical equipment and the service authorization are not necessarily the same thing.
.
Some commercially manufactured Starlink terminals have been authorized to operate using Starshield services. More specialized Starshield-only hardware also exists.
.
Ukraine’s Starshield contracts
Bloomberg reported on December 6, 2024, that the Pentagon had funded access to Starshield for:   500 Previously authorized terminals;  2,500 Additional terminals authorized, 3,000 terminals total.   (2024 contracts)
.
The additional 2,500 were existing Starlink terminals receiving upgraded Starshield access, not necessarily 2,500 newly manufactured military antennas. (/Bloomberg)
.
Ukraine’s Starshield contracts:
.
In September 2026, a United States Air Force procurement notice explicitly specified  Starshield Mini terminals, demonstrating that a smaller military-branded model exists. (https://t.co/O69fqY2Mju)
.
It would therefore be incorrect to argue that Ukraine cannot use Starshield aboard drones because military receivers are necessarily too heavy.
.
The unverified claim of Ukranian hacking of Starlink as an explanation for the data interruption cannot be accepted without additional evidence, especially given the earlier and distinct reports of Russian efforts to circumvent restrictions. (See more below.)
.
A January 31, 2026, report by the drone-industry publication DroneXL described an earlier situation in which Russian forces used Starlink terminals on attack drones.
.
Did Ukraine hack Starlink’s speed restriction?
This is where I found something particularly interesting.
.
There is a documented history of attempts to defeat Starlink speed restrictions, but the specific account I located concerns Russian operators rather than Ukrainian operators.
.

text:
🇭🇷🇺🇸 Honoring a legacy of service, sacrifice, and friendship.

Tonight in Eastlake, Ohio, Ambassador Pjer Šimunović opened the A250 exhibition Croatian Americans in the U.S. Armed Forces: History, Service, and Partnership at the American-Croatian Lodge Cardinal Stepinac, celebrating generations of Croatian Americans who have served in the United States Armed Forces and helped shape the story of their adopted homeland.

We were honored to welcome Representative David Joyce, Co-Chair of the Croatian Congressional Caucus, congressional candidate Maria Jukic, and Eastlake Mayor Kevin Kostelnik, who joined Ambassador Šimunović in delivering opening remarks.

Behind every name, photograph, and uniform is a story of courage, duty, and sacrifice. These are the stories of men and women who answered America’s call to serve, carrying with them a proud Croatian heritage while defending the ideals of their American home. Their contributions are a powerful reminder that the Croatian-American story is an inseparable part of the American story.

The bonds between Croatia and the United States are built not only through diplomacy and shared values, but also through generations of Croatian Americans who have served, sacrificed, and contributed to the nation they call home. Their legacy connects generations and strengthens the enduring friendship between our two nations.

As we mark America’s 250th anniversary, this exhibition offers an opportunity to remember those who served, honor the families who carry their legacy forward, and ensure that their stories are never forgotten.

Two nations, one enduring bond, and generations of service that remind us what it means to serve something greater than ourselves. 🇭🇷🤝🇺🇸

🥃🥃🥓🍗 BACON TO BUTTER CHICKEN, BLACK KNIGHT TO SINGLE MALT 🍗🥓🥃🥃

By: Bikash Mohanti

Times have changed. 
Armies have changed. 
Uniforms have changed. 
Waistlines, regrettably, have changed even more. And somewhere during this great march of progress, the Fauji palate staged a coup of its own.

Once upon a time, dinner at an Officers' Mess comprised smoked meat, salmon, dinner rolls, and soup served by a solemn bearer, the very summit of civilisation. Breakfast meant eggs, bacon, toast and coffee, preferably consumed while discussing matters of national importance, such as who had pinched the newspaper.

Then the counterattack began.
Dal Makhani infiltrated silently. Butter Chicken followed with armoured support. Naan and Roomali Roti outflanked the dinner roll, while Aloo-Puri and Aloo Paratha stormed breakfast, forcing bacon onto the defensive.
Coffee still holds some territory, but Chai (Tea) has occupied the headquarters. And frankly, nobody seems particularly anxious to liberate it.

Then came the more serious matter: Whisky.
When officers were dined in after commissioning in post-war days in 1971, 100 Pipers was the best in the bar. In those days, imported Scotch possessed something close to diplomatic immunity. A bottle was not merely opened. It was received with honours.
But supplies dwindled, as good things in the Army inevitably do.
Black Knight advanced to occupy the vacant ground. Then Red Knight arrived, followed by Solan No. 1, and eventually Peter Scot. 
Officers divided themselves into fiercely loyal camps. Arguments over which was superior occasionally became more tactically sophisticated than the day's training conference.
Peter Scot eventually established considerable authority over the Fauji liver. Then came the Indian-bottled blends: Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and 100 Pipers, among others. But the revolution was not finished.

Enter the single malt.
Suddenly the same officer who had once accepted whatever the Bar NCO poured into his glass began enquiring about age, region, peat, cask and finish.
Glenfiddich. Glenlivet.
The Fauji had become more than a whisky drinker.
He had become a consultant. Once whisky was poured over ice and consumed with soda. Today it is examined against the light, sniffed thoughtfully, rolled around the glass and discussed with an expression previously reserved for Corps Commanders' conferences.

Even the glass has been promoted.
The faithful Yera and Borosil tumblers, which had survived years of parties, postings, bachelors, married officers and Mess Secretaries, have increasingly surrendered their position to elegant crystal whisky glasses made in Ferozabad.
One suspects the whisky tastes better simply because the glass looks more expensive.

While the Indianisation of Army food proceeded magnificently, the whisky marched stubbornly in the opposite direction, all the way back to Scotland.
Our stomachs became increasingly Indian. Our whisky became increasingly Scottish.
No military appreciation has yet satisfactorily explained this manoeuvre.

The Rum Regiment, however, refused to retreat.
Rum drinkers are made of sterner stuff. They do not change allegiance merely because someone has discovered an eighteen-year-old single malt with notes of smoke, oak, honey and a Scottish hillside.
Hercules XXX had its loyalists. Then came Sea Pirate.

But towering over the battlefield was, and remains, Old Monk.
Old Monk is less a drink than a military institution. It has comforted generations of soldiers through cold nights, remote postings, wet canteens, bad weather and occasionally worse company.
Whenever rumours have circulated about its disappearance, the reaction has resembled the announcement that the pension has been abolished.
The faithful rally.
The bottles are checked.
Stocks are secured.
And civilisation survives.
The single-malt gentleman may discourse lovingly on his Speyside bouquet.
The Old Monk loyalist merely pours another and says:
"Achchha hai. Peeyo." (It's good. Just drink it)
A philosophy difficult to improve upon.

Beer, too, marched with the times.
Good old Golden Eagle once flew proudly over many a Mess gathering before Kingfisher displaced it and established a remarkably durable command.
Others appeared along the way: Rosy Pelican, Guru, Haywards and assorted hopefuls. Some arrived with fanfare and departed almost unnoticed, rather like certain staff appointments.
Now Foster's, Corona, Heineken and Budweiser share table space with Kingfisher.
The younger officer orders a beer by brand.
The older officer remembers when the principal criterion was:
"Thandi hai?" (Is it chilled?)
If the answer was yes, the selection process was complete.

And finally, dessert, where the Empire truly fell
Once upon a Mess table marched the great pudding battalions: Trifle, King George's Own V Pudding, Caramel Custard, Soufflés and their assorted relations.
Then came the indigenous offensive.
Rabri. Kheer. Ras Malai.
Resistance collapsed almost immediately.
Nobody called for artillery support.
Nobody demanded restoration of the old order.
Indeed, many of us quietly wondered why independence had taken so long to reach the dessert table.
And just as well.

So where does the Fauji palate march next?
I hesitate to predict.
By 2040, the Officers' Mess may well offer gluten-free quinoa parathas with organic Dal Makhani, while the bar produces a certificate explaining the ice cube's ancestry.
The young officer may ask: "Is the Butter Chicken ethically sourced?"
The Mess Havildar, representing several centuries of military common sense, will probably reply: "Sir, chicken hai." (Sir, it's chicken)

And somewhere in one corner will sit an ancient veteran, clutching his Old Monk, looking suspiciously at everybody and muttering: "In our time we didn't pair whisky with food. We paired it with another whisky."
And thus will the Indian Army march confidently into the future, honouring tradition while modifying the menu.

Armies may modernise, doctrines may change, uniforms may be redesigned, and technology may invade every headquarters… but the most enduring military operation remains the advance from the bar to the dinner table.

And unlike most operations we mounted in service, this one invariably achieved its objective.

text:
The first person to profit from a new oil discovery may be a landlord. The first person to feel poorer may be a tenant who owns no oil.

Commercial production can still be years away.

This is a timing problem that the usual celebration of resource wealth often misses. Future national income can change today's property prices, wages, borrowing and public commitments before the revenue is available to distribute.

A BIS paper published on 23 October investigates the price response to major discoveries before production begins. Its historical evidence motivates a broader question: how should a country manage claims on income that has not yet arrived?

The mechanism is easier to understand with an illustration.

A coastal town hears that an offshore field will be developed. Engineers and contractors are expected. A port may expand. The government announces infrastructure plans.

There are 1,000 suitable rental homes. Anticipated demand rises by 100, but new supply cannot appear immediately. Some adjustment therefore occurs through higher rents, greater occupancy or the displacement of existing tenants.

No petroleum revenue needs to have reached the local household for that household's living costs to rise.

The discovery can still be valuable. The issue is that future wealth and current capacity operate on different calendars.

This produces several economic tensions.

1. A valuable asset is not immediately available purchasing power for everyone.

Its present value depends on future production, prices, costs and risk. Borrowers may begin spending against that expectation. Domestic housing, skills and infrastructure take time to expand.

2. Local services cannot respond like imported goods.

A country can import equipment or consumer products, subject to financing and logistics. It cannot import a home already connected to the right local infrastructure in quite the same way.

Landowners and businesses serving the project may gain early. Workers in unrelated activities may experience rising costs before their income improves.

3. The exchange rate changes the route of adjustment.

A currency appreciation can make imports cheaper, while making life harder for domestic producers competing internationally. With a less flexible currency, more adjustment may occur through domestic wages and prices.

There is no exchange-rate arrangement that makes the underlying scarcity disappear.

4. Fiscal commitments can arrive before reliable fiscal revenue.

Some early investment is sensible. Better ports, power, training and administration can support development.

The harder problem is committing to permanent expenditure on the assumption that an optimistic project timetable and revenue forecast will be realised.

A hospital needs more than a construction budget. It needs staff, equipment, maintenance and operating finance for years. Future oil receipts must be assessed against the full commitment.

5. Different balance sheets can depend on the same forecast.

The government spends, banks lend, developers acquire land and households borrow. Each expects the project to transform income from a particular year.

A delay can then affect all of them together. Apparent diversification across borrowers conceals dependence on one common event.

This is why stress testing should ask what adjusts if production starts later, net receipts are smaller or international prices fall.

Contemporary comparisons also prevent an exaggerated conclusion.

Guyana is already producing oil, so it is not a clean pre-production experiment. But the IMF reports growth above 19% in 2025 alongside average inflation of 3.3%. Resource expansion does not automatically create an inflation crisis. Imports, savings, policy and capacity matter.

Suriname's IMF assessment highlights anticipated offshore development and substantial investment-related imports. It also identifies domestic policy slippages. A country awaiting oil can have inflation for several reasons; oil expectations should not become an explanation for everything.

Norway offers a different institutional lesson. Its framework separates petroleum receipts from the pace at which spending enters the domestic economy. The principle is to manage the conversion of a finite resource into lasting public wealth.

That framework cannot simply be copied into a country with different infrastructure needs or institutions. But the underlying distinction travels well: discovering wealth, earning cash and absorbing spending are separate stages.

My priority indicators would be rents, local service prices, resource and non-resource wages, property-related credit, and permanent spending commitments made before receipts arrive.

I would also examine the public-investment pipeline. Does spending expand capacity and future productivity, or mainly raise claims on already scarce workers and land?

The political challenge is distribution. A national GDP surge is unlikely to feel like shared prosperity if the first durable change for many families is an unaffordable home.

The objective should be to make the future windfall improve present choices without allowing present promises to consume the future in advance.

Good morning La Jungla 

The iron temple is behind me. The body has been worked; now it is time to feed it, to rest, and to sit with the games that come at noon.

What I observe instead is the endless murmuring of voices. Men stand upon their little platforms and speak as if words were steel, while the crowd gathers to nod and echo.

They never enter the temple. They never empty the mind or harden the body. They only trade insults across distance, each one demanding the respect that comes only from having been tested. It is amusing, in the way a shadows dance in a void. 
 In the flesh, none of them would last the length of a single breath. This is the old illusion: that the noise of the many can substitute for the discipline of the one.

 Those who drink from that cup remain thirsty, preferring the familiar poison of agreement over the quiet work of becoming something real.

The same pattern appears on the XRPL. Men call themselves keepers of the ledger while their true dealings stay in shadow.

 They offer salvation through speech alone. The cycles have already shown what such words are worth. Only those still new to the path believe them. The rest have learned that a ledger, like a sword, reveals the hand that holds it.

The way is simple. Speak less. Practice more. Empty the cup of other men’s noise and fill it with what you have actually done. Only then does the realm improve, because only then have you improved.

text:
WHEN PEACE MUST COME BEFORE THE OFFERING
When Jesus Taught That Reconciliation Matters Even at the Altar

Matthew 5:23–24 | NIV
THE WORSHIP GOD DESIRES
Imagine standing before God with an offering in your hands. Your heart is filled with worship. Yet suddenly, you remember someone you have wounded, a relationship damaged by your words, actions, or neglect.
What would Jesus tell you to do?

Astonishingly, He says to leave your offering, seek reconciliation, and then return to worship.

Jesus reveals a profound Kingdom truth: Our relationship with God cannot be separated from how we treat those He loves.

THE SERMON ON THE MOUNT
Jesus delivered this teaching during the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7), primarily instructing His disciples while crowds listened.
He had just declared that He came not to abolish the Law and the Prophets but to fulfill them (Matthew 5:17).

Then He addressed anger, contempt, and the commandment against murder. Jesus exposed the destructive attitudes from which outward wrongdoing can grow.

His listeners knew the importance of sacrifices at the Jerusalem temple. Bringing an offering was a solemn act of devotion.

Yet Jesus placed an urgent responsibility before the worshiper.

“First go and be reconciled to them; then come and offer your gift.” — Matthew 5:24 (NIV)

The startling command was not that sacrifice lacked value, but that genuine devotion required attention to broken relationships.

THE PERSON WHO HAS SOMETHING AGAINST YOU
Notice an easily overlooked detail.
Jesus does not say that you remember being angry with someone. He says you remember that another person has something against you.

The responsibility extends beyond managing our own resentment. It includes considering whether we have harmed someone else.

This requires humility.

We may need to acknowledge a careless word, an unfulfilled promise, an injustice, or an injury we have tried to forget.

Jesus calls us to take initiative instead of waiting for the wounded person to approach us.

The passage does not explain every circumstance or assign guilt automatically. Its central command is to pursue reconciliation sincerely.

WHY THE ALTAR COULD WAIT
Jesus was not declaring worship unimportant. He was revealing what authentic worship demands.
The prophets had already warned Israel against religious observances disconnected from righteousness and mercy.

Isaiah 1:11–17 calls God's people to turn from evil, seek justice, and defend the oppressed.

Micah 6:8 emphasizes justice, mercy, and humble fellowship with God.

Jesus brings these truths into the personal relationships of His disciples.

The offering could wait because the opportunity to repair a wounded relationship deserved immediate attention.

This is not a formula for earning God's acceptance. Reconciliation is a response to His grace, expressed through repentance, love, and obedience.

THE CROSS: GOD'S GREAT ACT OF RECONCILIATION
Jesus never demanded from humanity a love He was unwilling to demonstrate.
Through His death and resurrection, Christ accomplished what sinners could never achieve through their own righteousness.

Romans 5:8 reveals that Christ died for us while we were still sinners.

Second Corinthians 5:18 teaches that God reconciled us to Himself through Christ and entrusted believers with the ministry of reconciliation.

Here the Holy Trinity's work becomes beautifully evident: the Father initiates salvation, the Son accomplishes reconciliation through His sacrifice, and the Holy Spirit transforms believers to live in love and unity.

The peace Jesus commands reflects the reconciliation His grace makes possible.

PEACE WITHOUT PRETENDING
Reconciliation requires truth, not denial.
Jesus does not command believers to excuse wrongdoing, conceal abuse, or surrender wise boundaries.

Romans 12:18 instructs Christians to live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on them.

Sometimes an apology opens the door to renewed fellowship. Sometimes forgiveness is offered while trust must be rebuilt. Sometimes another person refuses peace.

Our responsibility is faithful obedience, not control over another person's response.

The Kingdom of Heaven advances through hearts willing to surrender pride, confess wrongdoing, extend mercy, and seek peace.

WHEN WORSHIP BECOMES A WAY OF LIFE
The altar in Matthew 5 was associated with temple sacrifice. Christians today approach God through Jesus Christ, whose sacrifice is sufficient and complete (Hebrews 10:10).
Nevertheless, the principle remains.

Before prayer, communion, or public worship, we should remain attentive to relationships needing repair.

A sincere apology may become an extraordinary act of obedience.

A humble conversation may demonstrate the Gospel more powerfully than impressive religious words.

Jesus teaches that love offered to God must shape the love we show our neighbor.

QUESTIONS FOR REFLECTION
Is there someone I have wounded whom God is calling me to approach with humility?
Have pride, fear, or self-justification prevented me from seeking peace?
Does my worship of Christ produce greater compassion, honesty, and reconciliation in my relationships?
CLOSING PRAYER
Heavenly Father, search my heart and reveal where pride, anger, or neglect has damaged my relationships. Lord Jesus, thank You for reconciling me to God through Your sacrifice. Teach me to follow Your example with humility and courage. Holy Spirit, soften my heart, guide my words, and give me wisdom to pursue peace without compromising truth. Help me forgive freely, acknowledge my wrongs sincerely, and love others as Christ has loved me. May my worship be genuine, my obedience joyful, and my life a testimony to Your reconciling grace. In the holy name of Jesus Christ, Amen.

Muhammad ﷺ met Jesus; Paul only saw a light
The majority of Muslim scholars hold that the Night Journey was in body and soul, because Allah says He took "His servant" (17:1), a word meaning the whole person. Muhammad ﷺ met Jesus face to face, spoke with him, and was greeted as "righteous brother and righteous prophet" (Bukhari 3207). He led Jesus and the prophets in prayer (Muslim 172).

Muhammad ﷺ described Jesus; Paul never did
The Prophet ﷺ described Jesus as of medium height, with a reddish complexion, as if he had just come out of a bath (Bukhari 3394). Paul never describes Jesus at all: only "a light from heaven" (Acts 26:13).

Muhammad's ﷺ claim was tested in public
When the Quraysh mocked his journey, they tested him on Jerusalem, a city he had never visited. Allah showed it to him and he described it in detail (Bukhari 3886; Muslim 170). Paul's companions "saw no man" (Acts 9:7), and no one could test his story.

And his prophethood doesn't rest on it
Paul's authority rests entirely on one vision. Muhammad's ﷺ rests on 23 years of public revelation, recited before thousands. The meeting with Jesus confirms his prophethood; it is not the foundation of it.

Why Muhammad ﷺ and not Paul

Muhammad ﷺ was foretold; Paul was warned against
Moses foretold a prophet "like unto thee" (Deuteronomy 18:18), and Jesus foretold "another Comforter" (John 14:16) named Ahmad (Quran 61:6). No prophet foretold Paul. Jesus warned against anyone claiming to have met him "in the desert" or "in the secret chambers" (Matthew 24:26).

Muhammad ﷺ kept the law; Paul ended it
Jesus came "not… to destroy the law" (Matthew 5:17). Muhammad ﷺ kept what Jesus kept: one God, prayer, fasting, circumcision, no pork (Leviticus 11:7; Quran 2:173). Paul said "Christ is the end of the law" (Romans 10:4).

Muhammad ﷺ kept Abraham's covenant
God made circumcision "an everlasting covenant" with Abraham (Genesis 17:13). Muslims keep it to this day. Paul said "if ye be circumcised, Christ shall profit you nothing" (Galatians 5:2). The Quran: "Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but upright in faith, a Muslim" (3:67).

Muhammad's ﷺ prophecies came true
Moses gave the test: if a prophet's word "follow not, nor come to pass," he is false (Deuteronomy 18:22). The Quran foretold that the defeated Romans would win again within a few years (30:2–4), and they did.

By their fruits
Jesus said "by their fruits ye shall know them" (Matthew 7:20). Muhammad's ﷺ fruit is worship of one God, as Jesus taught. Paul's fruit is a Jesus raised to God and a law set aside.

Comparing the apostles to Muhammad ﷺ

The apostles called Jesus a man; so did Muhammad ﷺ
Peter: "Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved of God… by miracles… which God did by him" (Acts 2:22). The Quran says the same: Jesus did miracles "by Allah's permission" (3:49).

The apostles kept the law; so did Muhammad ﷺ
The Jerusalem believers "are all zealous of the law" (Acts 21:20). Muslims keep God's law to this day.

The apostles' food laws are halal
The apostles commanded: "abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled" (Acts 15:29). The Quran forbids exactly these: blood, the strangled animal, and what is sacrificed to other than Allah (5:3). Paul said eat "whatsoever is sold in the shambles" (1 Corinthians 10:25).

The apostles prayed at set times; so do Muslims
"Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour" (Acts 3:1). "Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour" (Acts 10:9). Muslims pray five times a day at fixed times.

The apostles taught faith with works; so did Muhammad ﷺ
James: "by works a man is justified, and not by faith only" (James 2:24). The Quran repeatedly pairs "those who believe and do righteous deeds" (103:3).

text:
Some politicians and kings have found great joy in the strength of the LORD and have rejoiced in His salvation. However, many more have not.

Psalms 21:1 KJV The king shall joy in thy strength, O LORD; and in thy salvation how greatly shall he rejoice!

If Jesus Christ is the sole mediator between God and man, then all prayer should be in His Name.

1 Timothy 2:5 KJV For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;

When an unfabricated holocaust from God occurs, there are no debates or doubts.

One fruit is not like the other, no matter how hard you attempt to hyphenate them.

Psalms 21:9-10 KJV Thou shalt make them as a fiery oven in the time of thine anger: the LORD shall swallow them up in his wrath, and the fire shall devour them. Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth, and their seed from among the children of men.

The LORD has been exalted long before He created us, and I am just glad to now be a part of His worship team.

If it were not for the strength and power of the LORD, we would have no strength and power to praise and worship Him; this is why we glorify the power of the LORD and not our own.

Psalms 21:13 KJV Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength: so will we sing and praise thy power.

God is true to His promises even when we are not.

Genesis 21:1 KJV And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did unto Sarah as he had spoken.

God has amazed me many times, to the point that all I could do was laugh. God often laughs, and I enjoy laughing with Him.

Genesis 21:6 KJV And Sarah said, God hath made me to laugh, so that all that hear will laugh with me.

Men, with a divorce rate exceeding 50% even among Christian churches, what makes you think you could handle more than one wife, even if it were Biblically permissible? Like I said, God laughs, and I laugh with Him.

Genesis 21:9 KJV And Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, which she had born unto Abraham, mocking.

Genesis 21:10 KJV Wherefore she said unto Abraham, Cast out this bondwoman and her son: for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac.

Genesis 21:11 KJV And the thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight because of his son.

God heard the voice of the infant Ishmael and spoke with Hagar, the progenitors of a great nation. This nation includes the followers of Islam, who revere Jesus as a holy man, a prophet, and the Christ, yet do not believe in His deity or His death on the cross. How far God’s mercy and grace extend to them—as it did to Hagar and Ishmael—I do not know. All I know is that if I were in their shoes, I would not want to test the lengths and depths of such grace and mercy. Therefore, I will safely and by faith continue to proclaim Jesus for who He is: LORD, God, and King.

Genesis 21:16-17 KJV And she went, and sat her down over against him a good way off, as it were a bowshot: for she said, Let me not see the death of the child. And she sat over against him, and lift up her voice, and wept. And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.

If you walk faithfully with the LORD, even many of the heathen will come to respect it; however, no one respects a hypocrite.

Genesis 21:22 KJV And it came to pass at that time, that Abimelech and Phichol the chief captain of his host spake unto Abraham, saying, God is with thee in all that thou doest:

Abraham engaged in diplomacy with a Philistine king, highlighting the distinction between serving as an ambassador for the LORD and committing treason by forming alliances that declare an enemy of Christ to be the greatest ally.

Genesis 21:32 KJV Thus they made a covenant at Beersheba: then Abimelech rose up, and Phichol the chief captain of his host, and they returned into the land of the Philistines.

Jerusalem was the capital of Judah (the Jews) after the Kingdom of Israel was split. The Daughter of Zion is Jerusalem, which is why Jesus is referred to as the King of the Jews and why we, as spiritual descendants ('Jews' in Him by faith), say Christ is King.

Matthew 21:4 KJV All this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying,

Matthew 21:5 KJV Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.

David was a king of both Judah and Israel. Jesus, the Son of David, is the King of both Judah and Israel. There is no denying the Jewish lineage of Jesus. He was born among the worst to save the worst who trust in Him.

Matthew 21:9 KJV And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.

Imagine Jesus walking into a commercial, consumer-driven Christian church today.

If the amenities and entertainment were stripped from your church for just six months—reducing it to nothing but prayer and Bible study—how many people would remain for the duration and beyond? Your answer reveals whether you are part of a den of thieves or a house of prayer.

Matthew 21:12-13 KJV And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves, said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

As they are displeased today while attempting to usurp His throne.

Matthew 21:15 KJV And when the chief priests and scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children crying in the temple, and saying, Hosanna to the Son of David; they were sore displeased,

Many churches today have leaves with no fruit and then wonder why they wither away.

Matthew 21:19 KJV And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.

Matthew 21:20 KJV And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How soon is the fig tree withered away!

In accordance with the will of God, not our will.

Matthew 21:22 KJV And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.

John the Baptist had the respect of the people as a servant of the Word of God. Such men are rare today; those who have attained such stature through faithfulness are a great threat to the antichrist establishment.

Matthew 21:25 KJV The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why did ye not then believe him?

Matthew 21:26 KJV But if we shall say, Of men; we fear the people; for all hold John as a prophet.

Matthew 21:27 KJV And they answered Jesus, and said, We cannot tell. And he said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.

Lip action is not always synonymous with heart action that causes one to actually act. There is a short distance between heaven and hell, which is the distance between the mouth and the heart.

Matthew 21:28 KJV But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard.

Matthew 21:29 KJV He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.

Matthew 21:30 KJV And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.

Matthew 21:31 KJV Whether of them twain did the will of his father? They say unto him, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.

Matthew 21:32 KJV For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.

The nation from which the Kingdom of God has been taken is not our greatest ally.

Matthew 21:43 KJV Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.

Matthew 21:44 KJV And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.

Matthew 21:45 KJV And when the chief priests and Pharisees had heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.

May America fear such a multitude once again.

Matthew 21:46 KJV But when they sought to lay hands on him, they feared the multitude, because they took him for a prophet.

Jerusalem is a blessed city with Christ and a cursed city without Him.

Nehemiah 11:2 KJV And the people blessed all the men, that willingly offered themselves to dwell at Jerusalem.

I am not interested in a Golden Age. I am interested in the Kingdom Age.

Matthew 6:10 KJV Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

Father, we have found great joy in your strength and salvation. May we be the faithful ambassadors that you have called us to be. In Jesus’ Name, Amen.

🇺🇸 AFTER HOURS CITY REVIEW: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA

Los Angeles boasts one of America’s largest adult scenes, but 2026 reviews reveal a familiar problem: massive variety doesn’t guarantee quality, reliability or value.

💆 EROTIC MASSAGE

One of LA’s strongest categories, particularly around Torrance, Gardena and the South Bay. Reviews praise variety and individual experiences, but inconsistent quality, scheduling difficulties and management changes remain common complaints.

💎 KOREAN ESCORTS

A major LA strength, particularly around Koreatown, Downtown LA and Mid-Wilshire. Private accommodations and extensive selection are positives, but high prices, edited photos and inconsistent experiences remain concerns.

🇯🇵 JAPANESE ESCORTS

Another active market, with rotating lineups and mixed reviews. Some excellent experiences, but photo accuracy, communication and service consistency remain issues.

💃 STRIP CLUBS

Veterans reminisce about Deja Vu North Hollywood’s glory days. Its successor, Pink Diamonds, receives divided reviews, particularly regarding VIP pricing and atmosphere.

🌃 STREET SCENE

Figueroa and Western remain prominent in discussions, but reports highlight theft allegations, policing, safety concerns and unpredictable encounters.

📱 ONLINE & INDEPENDENTS

Independent listings offer variety but frequently draw complaints about misleading photos, unanswered messages and unreliable bookings. Agency website outages and changing names add confusion.

🍻 NIGHTLIFE & TOURISM

LA excels with Hollywood, beaches, restaurants, concerts, sports and nightlife. Traffic, sprawl and limited walkability are major drawbacks.

⚠️ THE BIGGER PICTURE

LA’s strengths are variety, organized agencies and established massage venues. Its weaknesses are inconsistent advertising, scheduling, pricing and geography. Firsthand reviews matter more than hype.

text:
A Philly landlord can fix the leak in a week and still be blocked from filing an eviction.

A property I work with there flagged this on a call this week, so I read the ordinance.
The city's Safe Healthy Homes Act takes effect on November 1st. If L&I cites a unit as unsafe or unfit, the owner gets a repair deadline of 30 days or less. Miss it and you can't collect rent until you're back in compliance. The tenant can also sue for $1,000 per violation, plus attorney fees.

Fix it on time and you're clear. Well not so fast…

In practice, "fixed" is a box an inspector checks. Your plumber can finish on day 6, and the violation stays open until L&I comes back. In 2024, the City Controller found L&I couldn't keep up with required reinspections on its most dangerous buildings.

An open violation also reaches further than you'd expect. To file an eviction after November 1, you'll need a city certificate issued within the last 30 days. The city won't issue one while a violation is open. The ceiling can be dry and the eviction still stuck.
There is a safe harbor for slow reinspections. It works as a defense inside a tenant's lawsuit, and the owner carries the proof.

Philly isn't alone. Bisnow ran a piece this week on habitability claims surging in eviction courts across the country. More tenants have lawyers than ever. One LA landlord attorney says AI lets tenants produce the paperwork almost instantly, and he puts a full trial at up to $150,000. A California manager with 2,000 units now offers two months' free rent just to avoid filing.

Eviction counts are dropping. Both sides agree that part of the drop is settlements that never become filings.

Tenant advocates have their own numbers. In Cleveland, about 76% of tenants with right-to-counsel lawyers reported defective conditions in their homes. Some landlords earned this law.

But Philadelphia wrote a rule where the clock runs on two crews: the owner's and the city's. Only one of them carries the risk when the clock runs out.

It's unlikely the ACC will be able to poach from the Big 12 for three reasons:

(1) The Big 12's next TV contract will start in July 2032, a year before the ACC's exclusive negotiation window with ESPN opens.  At that point in time, the Big 12's Grant of Rights will be extended.

(2) All Big 12 members are signers of the Big 12's bylaws, which state in section 1.2.3. that "each Member agrees with the Conference and with each of the other Members to remain a member of the Conference for ninety-nine (99) years beginning July 1, 2012."  The bylaws go on to breakdown the exit fee, which is substantial.

(3) The Big 12 has little risk of ever being poached.  And, there are no members actively pining & strategizing to leave.  Simply put, it's a more stable league.  No Big 12 team is going to want to pay 9 figures to buyout the GOR & exit the conference to join a league that has multiple members trying to figure out how to leave for more money.

The Big 12 is the one that's set up to poach from the ACC.  They'll be able to offer any ACC team significantly more money a year before those teams will be able to see what the ACC is worth.  And, they'll be able to offer stability & elite basketball to boot.  They don't even have to go after the most premier brands.  They could easily target someone like Louisville.  Like the Big 12 targeting Colorado in order to weaken the Pac-12, poaching a team like Louisville would undermine the conference & prompt the premier brands to consider making a conference move.

text:
The Monroe Doctrine. You might have heard about it but allow me, Thomas Jefferson, to show you the background. You look back upon the year 1823 as a time when the United States finally grew into its sovereignty, marked by the declaration that now bears the name of my dear friend, James Monroe. You know it as a doctrine that barred European empires from western shores. But let me pull back the curtain of history to show you how the ghost of our revolutionary ideals—and my own hand—guided that fateful pen.

In the autumn of that year, a urgent packet arrived here at Monticello from President Monroe. The weight of the world was upon his shoulders. The Spanish colonies to our south had heroically broken their chains, establishing independent republics modeled after our own. Yet, the absolute monarchs of Europe—the so-called Holy Alliance—were gathering like vultures, eager to cross the Atlantic and drag those free spirits back into subjugation. To complicate matters, Great Britain had approached us with a proposal: a joint declaration to warn the monarchs away. Monroe asked for my counsel.

My reply to him was immediate, for I recognized this as the most momentous question since that of our own Independence. That declaration made us a nation; this decision would set our compass for centuries to come.

I advised Monroe that our first and fundamental maxim should be never to entangle ourselves in the broils of Europe. Our second, never to suffer Europe to intermeddle with cis-Atlantic affairs.
America, North and South, has a set of interests distinct from those of the Old World. While Europe is laboring to become the domicile of despotism, our endeavor must be to make our hemisphere that of freedom. This "Two-Spheres" philosophy is an idea I championed my entire life. The political systems of Europe, built on hereditary crowns and perpetual warfare, have no business in the Americas, where the rights of man are taking root.

Now, history notes a curious irony. I actually urged Monroe to accept the British offer. You may find this surprising, given that I spent my life fighting British imperialism. But I was a realist. I knew the British Navy was the most powerful force on the globe. By aligning with them, we would place that massive naval shield over the entire hemisphere, stopping the Holy Alliance without the United States firing a single shot.

As you know, Monroe ultimately chose a more independent path. His brilliant Secretary of State, John Quincy Adams, argued that we should not follow like a small boat in the wake of a British warship. He believed the United States should speak for itself, boldly and alone. Monroe agreed, and the doctrine was issued as a unilateral American stance.

Though Monroe rejected my tactical advice to ally with Britain, he fully adopted the strategic architecture I laid out. The core of the Monroe Doctrine is pure Jeffersonian thought: a political and philosophical boundary drawn down the center of the Atlantic Ocean.

We forced the Old World to stay on its side of the deep, so that the flame of liberty could safely burn on ours.

text:
Thomas Aquinas and Karl Barth: 
An Unofficial Catholic-Protestant Dialogue 
Edited by Bruce L. McCormack and Thomas Joseph White, O.P.
Chapters under review: 
▪️“Barth and Aquinas on Election, Relationship, and Requirement” by John R. Bowlin
▪️“Divine Action and Human Action in St. Thomas Aquinas: An Analogia Legis” by Holly Taylor Coolman
→ 
{{Multiple A.I. Reviews Argued Against One Another To Resolution & Synthesis}}
→ 
The material consists of John R. Bowlin’s “Barth and Aquinas on Election, Relationship, and Requirement” (pp. 237–261) and Holly Taylor Coolman’s “Divine Action and Human Action in St. Thomas Aquinas: An Analogia Legis” (pp. 262–279). 

Both are tightly focused comparative essays that treat election, grace, obligation, and divine-human action through shared conceptual resources (a social theory of obligation for Bowlin; the analogical scope of lex in ST I-II, qq. 90–108 for Coolman) rather than through the classic loci on predestination, sufficient and efficacious grace, or the relation of decree to foreknowledge.

Bowlin:
Bowlin begins from a Hegelian premise (that negation specifies concepts more determinately than bare similarity) and argues that the most useful comparison of Aquinas and Barth on election attends to differences set against a shared backdrop. That backdrop is a social theory of obligation: requirements arise within relationships (especially friendship), are warranted by the goodness of the relationship, and are justly binding only when the relationship itself is good. Both theologians assume this structure. Divine action creates human obligation by establishing a friendship of mutual love; love becomes law without arriving as an alien constraint on the will.

He documents the shared concern directly. Aquinas (ST II-II, q. 23, a. 2; q. 44, a. 1) insists that the Spirit orders all things suaviter and that love’s requirements “cannot be fulfilled except out of one’s very own will.” Barth (CD IV/2, pp. 579–80) likewise rejects an abstract law that has no locus in a life fulfilling it and that merely advances an arid claim. The sources of the concern differ (Barth’s modern drama of self-determination and Kantian/Hegelian anxieties; Aquinas’s natural/supernatural relations), and the replies differ (righteousness re-created in humanity for Thomas; righteousness belonging most basically to Christ for Barth), yet the theory of obligation itself is identical.

Bowlin then executes four tasks. First he spells out the logic of relationship and requirement (roles, expectations, justice as what is due, the need for reasons that value the relationship rightly, and practices of mutual assessment that yoke authority to willingness to obey). Obedience to a just demand expresses belonging and generates positive freedom; the requirements arrive as gifts. Friendship is the paradigm: sacrifice creates or deepens the union and thereby generates its requirements. 

Second, he recounts Barth’s doubts about applying this logic to human relationships. Any claim to know the good (whether by created nature or re-creating grace) yields only a semblance of obligation, not a real order that binds categorically. The result is master/slave dynamics or Nietzschean suspicion. 

Third, Barth’s response is the Christological rendering: in Jesus Christ “God elects Himself to be gracious toward man” (CD II/2, p. 510). Jesus is both electing God and elected man; all humanity exists as predicate of this divine Subject. The good is done on our behalf; the relationship consists in God accepting man out of pure free compassion; the aim is friendship and fellowship. Requirements (love of Jesus and neighbor) follow as the recognition and endorsement of what has already been accomplished. 

Fourth, he notes the burdens: Barth’s actualism (command always concrete, never known in advance) and hyper-Augustinian opacity of the good quoad nos leave temporal obligations uncertain and criticism vulnerable to voluntarism. The perfect union of authority and freedom remains largely eschatological promise. By contrast, Aquinas’s infused virtues and the Spirit’s gifts re-create judgments and loves into (fragile, Spirit-dependent) habits that enable relatively constant critical practice.

The essay closes by suggesting that a thoroughly modern account of the virtues (both acquired and infused) could retain traditional claims about justification and the moral consequences of election while avoiding both hyper-Augustinian exaggeration and the Kantian/Nietzschean constraints that shaped Barth’s path. 

Strengths are the clarity with which the shared social theory is isolated, the precise mapping of differences in source and reply, and the honest registration of Barth’s burdens.

The principal limitation relative to grace and conversion is that the chapter treats election as the gracious constitution of friendship in Christ; it does not engage the classic mechanics of who receives the grace that effects conversion, whether any grace is withheld, or the relation of decree to foreknowledge.

Coolman:
Coolman uses the treatise on law (ST I-II, qq. 90–108) as an entry into divine and human action. Lex is not a narrow juridical category but a sweeping analogical reality: everything is ordered according to the eternal law (God’s own reason, not distinct from Himself). She unfolds five forms—eternal, natural, human, and divine (Old and New)—to display the relationship between divine and human action with a coherence and nuance not available in any single section.

Eternal law is the foundation (Supreme Reason, the logical correlate of Providence). It is appropriated to the Son; Christ “is himself the eternal law” by appropriation (ST I-II, q. 93, a. 4). The analogia legis is therefore an analogia Christi that precedes and encompasses both creation and redemption. Natural law is the participation of practical reason in the eternal law (first principle: good is to be done and evil avoided). It constitutes human action as human, survives the Fall, and remains an unbreakable form of participation in Christ. 

This produces a real disagreement with Barth, who treats sinful humanity as having revoked access to creation as such. Human law, derived from natural law and binding only when ordered to the common good and properly promulgated, ennobles practical reason and supplies a category in which the actions of non-Christians can be accounted relatively good—again a challenge to Barth. 

Divine law (Old and New) moves humanity beyond natural faculties to the vision of God and friendship with God. The New adds nothing in substance or in the moral precepts; it is the Old “in translation.” Its distinctive form is “chiefly the grace itself of the Holy Ghost, which is given to those who believe in Christ” (ST I-II, q. 106, a. 1). The Spirit’s work is perfect promulgation: the law is written on the heart so that it is both indicated and accomplished in compliance with the person’s own will (the law of liberty). Christ is both foundation and telos; the culminating form is also pneumatological.

Coolman notes that Aquinas’s distinctions among intensities of participation (some only in natural and human law, others in the fullness of the New Law) are foreign to Barth, yet the shared Christological grounding of the relation between humanity and God, together with the pneumatological character of the New Law, offers points of convergence. Strengths are the careful reading of the treatise as a unified whole, the explicit Christological appropriation of eternal law, and the practical implications for pluralistic collaboration. 

Like Bowlin’s chapter, it does not address the mechanics of grace’s distribution, withholding, or the ground of election in foreknowledge versus decree.

In Bowlin’s presentation of Barth, election is the act in which God elects Himself to be gracious toward man in Jesus Christ. All of humanity exists as predicate of this divine Subject; the good is done on our behalf out of pure free compassion; the relationship of friendship is initiated by that grace. The human response is faith’s recognition and endorsement of what has already been accomplished. No grace is portrayed as withheld prior to conversion; the election itself is the gracious act that creates the friendship. 

The chapter’s actualism and hyper-Augustinian notes concern the opacity of the good on the horizontal plane and the concrete character of command, not a prior withholding of converting grace.

In both chapters’ presentation of Aquinas, grace establishes the friendship of charity (Bowlin) and the New Law is “chiefly the grace itself of the Holy Ghost” given to those who believe (Coolman). The command arrives suaviter, enabling what it commands and fulfilling it from the person’s own will. 

Coolman explicitly allows different intensities of participation in the analogia legis: some remain at the level of natural and human law, while others participate in the New Law. This may or may not imply that the full grace of the Spirit that constitutes friendship with God and the law of liberty is not received by all. 

For Barth (as read by Bowlin), the single gracious election in Christ, together with the Spirit’s direction, is what creates the relationship and enables the faithful response. 

For Aquinas (as read by both), the Spirit’s grace that constitutes the New Law is itself what re-creates the person, writes the law on the heart, and enables the response of love and obedience. 

The initiating grace of the relationship or friendship and the grace that perfects the response are not separated into two distinct grants in these essays.

The chapters treat election and the New Law as the gracious constitution of friendship and as the pneumatological perfection of law. 

The differences they do emphasize concern the sources of the shared concern about non-alien obligation, the presence or absence of a natural-law category, the relative constancy of re-created judgment, and the intensities of participation in the analogia legis.

End.

Sitting at -11.5 keeps you well below the dangerous two-touchdown margin of 14, requiring Tech to win by 12 points against a Cincinnati front struggling to defend perimeter zone-read concepts.

​Floyd of Rosedale Trenches: Iowa’s defense is allowing just 14.5 points per game and under 85 yards rushing on the ground. Minnesota’s offense relies on establishing interior push; when forced into obvious passing downs against Iowa’s secondary and edge rushers, drives stall quickly. If Iowa forces one short-field turnover, they have the script to cover the touchdown hook.

​8. BYU -7.5 (-104) at UCF (3:30 PM ET)
​Turnover Variance: BYU's ball-control offense excels at avoiding negative plays and sacks, while UCF's aggressive defensive front is prone to giving up chunk plays on missed run fits. Laying just over a touchdown with BYU's red-zone conversion rate offers strong value.

​9. North Texas at Navy — OVER 62.5 (-106) (3:30 PM ET)
​Explosive Tempo vs. Option Efficiency: While Navy will control clock on the ground, North Texas features one of the fastest, most aggressive aerial attacks in the country capable of scoring in under two minutes. Navy's defense will struggle to prevent chunk pass plays, forcing a back-and-forth track meet in Annapolis.  

​10. Houston at Utah — OVER 56.5 (-110) (10:15 PM ET)
​Late-Night Shootout Script: Utah home games in October have heavily trended Over (hitting in 8 of the last 9 as a favorite). text:
Annie Edson Taylor: The 63-Year-Old Schoolteacher Who Became the First Person to Survive Niagara Falls in a Barrel

On October 24, 1901—her 63rd birthday—Annie Edson Taylor, a schoolteacher from Auburn, New York, climbed into a custom oak-and-iron barrel and became the first person to survive a plunge over Niagara Falls. 

Taylor was born Annie M. Edson on October 24, 1838, in Auburn, New York, one of eight children of a flour mill owner. Widowed early after her husband David Taylor died in the Civil War and their infant son passed away, she worked as a schoolteacher and later attempted to teach music and dance, including opening a school in Bay City, Michigan. Financial setbacks, including a house fire and lost investments, left her seeking a bold way to secure her future amid the tourist boom around the 1901 Pan-American Exposition in nearby Buffalo. 

The idea struck her while reading about visitors to the falls: no one had gone over Niagara in a barrel and lived. She designed (and had built) a sturdy barrel of white Kentucky oak bound by iron hoops, roughly 4½ to 5 feet tall and about 3 feet in diameter, weighing around 160 pounds. It was padded inside with a mattress and cushions, included a harness or grips for support, and carried a heavy anvil (reported variously around 100–200 pounds) as ballast to help keep it upright. She also brought a lucky heart-shaped pillow. Two days earlier, a domestic cat was sent over the Horseshoe Falls in the barrel as a test; the cat survived with a head injury and later posed with Taylor in photographs. 

On the afternoon of her birthday, the barrel was launched from a rowboat near Grass Island (south of Goat Island) on the American side. Taylor entered, the lid was screwed down, air was compressed with a bicycle tire pump and sealed with a cork, and she was set adrift. Currents carried her through the rapids and over the Canadian Horseshoe Falls (the largest of the three waterfalls, with a drop of roughly 160–170 feet). The barrel went over around 4:23 p.m., resurfaced quickly, and was recovered about 17 minutes later near the base. Rescuers, including fellow daredevil Carlisle Graham, opened it and found Taylor alive. She suffered a gash on her head (or behind her ear), bruises, and shock but no broken bones and was able to walk. 

She later warned others against the stunt, saying she would “sooner walk up to the mouth of a cannon, knowing it was going to blow me to pieces than make another trip over the Fall.” 

Fame proved fleeting. Taylor (who had publicly claimed to be in her 40s) gave talks, sold a short memoir, and posed for tourist photos as the “Queen of the Mist,” but unscrupulous managers allegedly took advantage of her, and her barrel was stolen more than once. She never achieved the financial security she sought, later worked as a clairvoyant or offered magnetic treatments, and entered the Niagara County Infirmary in Lockport in 1921. She died there on April 29, 1921, at age 82, and was buried in the “Stunter’s Rest” section of Oakwood Cemetery in Niagara Falls next to Carlisle Graham. 

Taylor’s feat made her a lasting symbol of Niagara’s daredevil history. While later attempts (mostly by men) followed at the Horseshoe Falls, she remains the first documented survivor and the only woman to have gone over alone in that era. Her story highlights both the allure and the risks of early 20th-century stunts driven by economic pressure and the desire for notoriety. 

Modern views of the Horseshoe Falls still evoke the power of the cataract she conquered.

To ALL uninformed people buying into the radical left democrat socialists/muslims-THIS is exactly what you get from "free" healthcare-FYI the UK also has almost the same bad healthcare!! GET INFORMED before letting commies give you FALSE pipe dreams THAT NEVER HAPPEN!!
Nina David · ·
For those who think that universal healthcare or Medicare for all is the way to go, please read the following. Canada has what your asking for and it isn't a good thing.
This was a friend's experience.
Most of you know I spent 4 days in the hospital in Nova Scotia Canada and I wanted to share my experience with Universal Healthcare.
📷 an ambulance with two very nice paramedics met me on my cruise ship and escorted me to the hospital.  We entered into a very long hallway where there were approximately 25 other patients in gurneys waiting to be seen by an emergency room doctor. I thanked the paramedics for getting me to the ER as I assumed they would be dropping me off and be on to their next call! That’s how we do it in the USA anyway.  They politely explained to me that they would not be leaving my side until I was actually seen by a doctor, which could take several hours as they might be needed to administer any life saving measures in the meantime.  They explained that healthcare is “free” in Canada to Canadian Citizens and that they can’t recruit doctors to work for them due to the high taxes and the low pay.  They told me to prepare for a long night.  Okay…… I started to realize I wasn’t in Kansas anymore.
It was a cold and rainy night and it was absolutely freezing in that hallway. I’m so sick and miserable being strapped in that gurney.  The hallways were crowded with us 25 + patients and at least 50 paramedics all staying with their patients.  To pass the time, the paramedics spent most of their time laughing and visiting with the other paramedics.  The lead paramedic was looking over my medical chart from the ship doctor and saw that he suggested I needed a CT scan.  He looked at me and said “I just want to prepare you that you may not get a CT scan for 2 or 3 days!”  2 or 3 days? WTH! At that point I pulled out my phone to see how far away I was from the nearest U.S. hospital…. 8 hours by car! I didn’t think I could do it and I felt stuck.
At  3 a.m. I am finally seen by a doctor and was told they would be admitting me.  They take me to my room and I’m so thankful to be off that gurney!  I look around the small room and I don’t see a bathroom.  I know the nearest bathroom is a long ways down the hallway and I don’t think I can make it by walking.  I call the nurse for a wheelchair when she tells me if it’s an emergency I can use the one in the room.  She opens up a cabinet and pulls out a toilet.  Are you kidding me? Well when you gotta go…. Sitting there with absolutely no privacy some random guy walks in my room!  Ugh! Poor guy! 📷
The next morning the doctor told me I needed to see a Urologist and he was at another hospital so I would need to be transferred there.  Thank you God! I’m getting out of this 3rd world excuse for a hospital.
The outside of the building looks decent, maybe things are looking up!  As I’m being taken to the 7th floor I’m paying close attention.  The hallways are filled with cardboard boxes, random equipment and supplies and appears to be mostly used as storage.  I pass several patient rooms and I can see that each small room has 4 patients in each one, divided by 4 curtains.  My heart sinks.
As they take me to my room my attendant told me I was in luck and I would have a private room since I had insurance and was a “paying customer” Whew!  I look around the small room and see a bathroom!  Oh yay! 
They also inform me “DO NOT” drink the water, don’t brush your teeth with it and don’t shower in it.  I look in my bathroom and sure enough the shower parts  were pulled out of the wall.  Right now I could care less about a shower!
At this point things are becoming a blur.  I only had to wait a couple of days for my CT scan and was able to get to the operating room to get a stent put in that the Urologist says I needed right away. As I’m wheeled to the operating room, the sheet I’m sitting on falls partially on the floor and when I get there, I look down and see the white sheet is absolutely filthy dirty.  I don’t know how often they mop those floors, but it’s obviously not often.  Do I really want them doing anything to me?  Doesn’t seem very sterile. The interior of the hospital is in disrepair.  Drywall falling off the walls, broken tiles, and filthy dirty!
Get back to my room and it’s pleasant enough, at least I have a window!  There is not a T.V. and no internet, so the days were very long. Luckily a nice nurse brought in a recliner so Ed was able to stay with me in my room.  Good thing as there were very few hotel rooms available and they were in the $700 a night range!
The food was fair, and you were able to order from a menu.  The breakfast menu didn’t offer any eggs or meat.  French toast it is, served cold of course! The next morning I ordered a “high protein” banana smoothie, should be safe.  Wrong!  I don’t know what was in that 4 ounce smoothie, but I wasn’t trying it!
The nurses were nice enough, they didn’t bother you very much.  I usually saw them twice per day, during shift changes.  On day 3, I really need a bath and my linens changed.  I asked a nurse for help.  Lucky me, since I didn’t have an open wound, I could have a shower!  Yay me!  She led me down the hallway and opened what looked like a closet door.  She handed me a small plastic container that contained a couple of dingy, tattered wash cloths and a towel the size of a standard kitchen towel.  All well, I’ll take it.
My last day a cleaning lady came to “clean” my room.  I don’t know why she even bothered.  She didn’t empty the trash, which was a large container that was more than halfway full.  Had to be there long before I came in.  What really shocked me was the Haz Mat container.  The container was not enclosed and was full of used syringes, bloody equipment, etc.  I just about barfed every time I walked by it.
I am thankful for the care I received. The doctors seemed knowledgeable and I did get better.  They did not seem in a hurry to discharge me and I’m assuming that was partly due to my ability to pay.  I feel really sorry for the Canadian’s that have to deal with this.  We were told that a lot of them travel to the U.S. for their healthcare.  I can NOW see why.
I also realize that we need some reform with our American healthcare, but trust me, Universal Healthcare run by red taped government bureaucrats is not the way to go!  I’m amazed by the number of Americans who want this!  Sounds good until you actually have to live it!  I’m so thankful that I’m not a Canadian, because I would probably still be there!
The next time I visit our Montrose Regional Hospital I’m going to kiss the walls!

text:
💉👵 Grandparents share polio memories to remind families why vaccines matter

📰 What's the story?

Dr Arthur Lavin is a retired children's doctor from Ohio and the co-founder of Grandparents for Vaccines (Rotary).
The group was founded in September 2025 and has nearly 6,000 members in more than 30 US states.
Members share real memories of life before vaccines, when polio, measles and whooping cough could kill or disable children. They do it through letters, talks and short videos on TikTok and Instagram (North Jersey).
As one volunteer puts it: "We don't debate. We narrate."
💔 One grandmother's story
Beth Summer from Florida shared the story of her brother, Whizzer. He caught polio in 1954, when he was 16 and a star football player.
He was paralysed and had almost 30 operations. He walked again only with a heavy brace and crutches, and missed graduating with his classmates.

In later life he developed post-polio syndrome and needed a wheelchair. He died in 2020, aged 81.
Beth says: "Our children are our future, and we cannot abandon our obligations to them."
🌍 Where polio stands today
Polio is close to being wiped out, but Rotary warns that "99.9% is not 100%". Wild polio is still found in Afghanistan and Pakistan (Rotary Club of Ann Arbor).
In the US, vaccination rates are falling and measles has come back.

⚖️ Both sides
Supporters say real stories reach people in ways statistics can't, and help bring vaccination rates back up.
Some parents still have questions or worries about vaccines. The group says it wants to listen and reassure them, not lecture them.
💬 My view
Huge thanks to Rotary and the grandparents sharing such painful memories. 🙏 Stories like Whizzer's remind us that polio wasn't just a word in a history book. It changed whole lives. Vaccines are one of the greatest gifts science has given our children. If you have questions, talk to your GP or practice nurse. Here in the UK, the NHS offers vaccines free to every child. Let's finish the job and #EndPolio for good. 💙

🗳️ Poll: Do you remember a family story about polio or other childhood diseases?
🟢 Yes, my family has one
🔴 No
🤔 I'll ask my grandparents

text:
The United States military now needs Elon Musk's PERMISSION to go to space.

SpaceX turned down three Space Force missions, and not one other rocket company offered to take them.

12 years ago, SpaceX sued the government to break a launch monopoly. Now SpaceX is the monopoly, and this week showed what that means:

In April 2014, SpaceX went to court because the Air Force had handed United Launch Alliance a sole-source block buy of 36 rocket cores for national security launches. 

Elon's argument was simple: Military launches should be competed, and if SpaceX competed and lost, that was fine. ULA was flying on Russian-made engines at the time, and Elon made sure everyone knew it.

Today, the board looks like this:

SpaceX flew 85% of American launches in 2025. ULA's Vulcan was grounded this year after booster problems. Blue Origin's New Glenn exploded on its only Florida launch pad in May and is likely out until next year. Launch capacity is now the binding constraint for the whole industry, and Seraphim doesn't expect relief before 2029.

Federal law tells the Pentagon to sustain at least two launch vehicles that can deliver any national security payload. For these three missions, the number of companies willing to fly them was zero.

And then there's SpaceX's own AI business:

It brought in $7.5 billion of the company's $14.6 billion in revenue last quarter, and SpaceX's 2027 Starship flights are focused on Starlink V3 and prototype data centers. SpaceX is also phasing out Falcon 9, and many military satellites don't fit on Starship. 

So the scarcest thing in space, a ride to orbit, now belongs to a company with its own AI satellites to launch.

And the same man is reportedly being brought onto a Pentagon commission on the future of warfare, which nine current and former officials told Politico raises conflict-of-interest concerns.

But Elon didn't break any rule here. 

A private company is allowed to turn down a customer, and that's the whole problem. Washington let national security depend on a company that's free to say no.

SpaceX earned this position by being cheaper and better than everyone else, and the failures at ULA and Blue Origin aren't Elon's fault. A Space Force general also says the gaps are temporary and the military is working through them.

But if launch is now national-security infrastructure, it should be treated that way: 

Any company holding most of the launch capacity should have to reserve a share of it for national security missions. The Pentagon should pay to keep a second provider flying even when it costs more, because that's what the law already demands. And no launch provider should help write the Pentagon's plans for the future of war.

SpaceX won the fight it started in 2014, and the prize turned out to be the Pentagon's dependence.
