text:
🇰🇵|DANDONG 12 YEAR BRIDGE WAKES UP: KIM CROSSES, LAYS WREATH, TURNS BACK, AND CARGO TAKES OVER

A BRIDGE LEFT IDLE FOR TWELVE YEARS AND A FLASH VISIT BY KIM JONG UN

October 24, 2026, Dandong. Kim Jong Un crosses New Yalu River Bridge.

Wang Huning greets him at bridgehead, conveying regards from Xi Jinping. Kim Jong Un lays floral tribute at Monument to War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, and tours automobile factory. That evening, Wang Huning sees him off at bridgehead. He does not travel to Beijing at any point during visit. Thirteen months earlier, on previous trip to China, he had gone to Beijing to meet Xi Jinping. This time, he traveled only as far as Dandong, staying for just few hours.

Every detail of visit serves as signal. Most significant signal is bridge itself.

TWELVE YEARS OF A BRIDGE: FROM EXPENSIVE DEAD END TO STRATEGIC SWITCH

Completed in 2014, New Yalu River Bridge, four lane, 3026 meter long structure, was funded by China at cost of approximately 310 million dollars. Starting from Dandong, it spans Yalu River only to come to abrupt halt, ending on patch of dirt on outskirts of Sinuiju, North Korea. This is because connecting roads and customs facilities on North Korean side were never built.

For twelve years, bridge has stood as exceedingly expensive dead end. It carries no cargo. It transports no passengers. It simply remains in place, like frozen question mark.

Why was it left in limbo. North Korea nuclear tests. Harsh UN Security Council sanctions of 2017, for which Beijing voted in favor. Kim Jong Un border closures during pandemic. Pyongyang wariness of becoming overly dependent on China economically. Each factor compounded, transforming bridge from symbol of cooperation into monument to mutual distrust.

Why open it now. Because Beijing calculations have shifted. Term denuclearization has vanished from China public facing diplomacy regarding North Korea. North Korea nuclear arsenal is no longer viewed merely as proliferation risk, but rather as durable buffer capable of pinning down US military attention. Once Beijing accepts nuclear armed North Korea as baseline reality, maintaining stranglehold on North primary commercial arteries loses strategic rationale.

Opening of bridge is not friendly gesture. Opening is strategic decision. Beijing uses concrete and roadways to anchor North Korea firmly in place.

WHY DID KIM JONG UN STOP IN DANDONG INSTEAD OF TRAVELING TO BEIJING

He visited Dandong because October 25 marks anniversary of Chinese People Volunteers CPV entering Korean War. By laying floral tribute, he honored martyrs of War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea. Ribbon bore inscription in Korean: Forever Remember Martyrs of Chinese People Volunteers. He also toured Memorial Hall of War to Resist US Aggression and Aid Korea, presenting historical photograph inscribed in his own hand.

This was carefully calibrated gesture, not plea for economic aid, but reaffirmation of historical bonds. In year marking 65th anniversary of Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance between DPRK and China, and on eve of 76th anniversary of CPV entry into conflict, Kim Jong Un stood in Dandong. Through commemoration of martyrs, he reminded Beijing: we are bound by treaty written in blood, shared history, and relationship that no third party can replace.

Yet he did not go to Beijing. He met with Wang Huning, member of Politburo Standing Committee ranked fourth, occupying precise position: below absolute top leadership, yet above secondary tier. Arrangement signals that while relationship is warming, it has not yet reached level of direct, top tier alignment. Kim Jong Un signals, I need you, while simultaneously asserting, I will not kneel. To domestic audience, he conveys that he has not been subsumed. To Beijing, he signals, I am here, but I am keeping distance.

TWO BRIDGES AND A 98 PERCENT BILL

Just five weeks before opening of New Yalu River Bridge, road bridge spanning Tumen River, connecting North Korea and Russia, was opened on September 7, 2026. From start of construction to ribbon cutting ceremony, bridge took only about 16 months to complete. Compared to twelve year timeline for project over Yalu River, pace in context of Moscow resembles wartime sprint.

On surface, Kim Jong Un appears to be playing Russia card. He leverages military partnership with Putin to compel China to re engage. Yet economic gravity remains indifferent to such optics.

China accounts for over 98 percent of North Korea recorded foreign trade. In 2025, trade between two nations reached approximately 2.735 billion dollars, year on year increase of more than 25 percent, recovering to 98.1 percent of pre pandemic levels. In first half of 2026, trade volume hit roughly 1.5 billion dollars, marking another increase of nearly 20 percent. City of Dandong alone handles more than 70 percent of all China North Korea trade.

Russia can offer North Korea security guarantees, fuel, food, and battlefield technology, in exchange for artillery shells and troops. However Russia cannot replace China role as North Korea economic lifeline. Speed at which bridge is built cannot alter weight of nation economic reality. Kim Jong Un may walk tightrope between Moscow and Beijing, but wire beneath feet is anchored in Chinese concrete.

WASHINGTON CONCERNS AND BLUNTED LEVERAGE

Upon bridge opening, US State Department remarked: Increased cross border trade should not facilitate sanctions evasion or support DPRK illicit weapons programs.

Phrasing itself betrays sense of powerlessness. It is not declaration of we will not permit this, but rather statement that this should not happen. It is plea, not prohibition, because primary lever at Washington disposal, sanctions, is losing edge. Through military cooperation with Russia, North Korea has secured credible alternative. As Washington most potent bargaining chip, sanctions relief, depreciates in value, calls for Beijing to ensure trade is not used to circumvent sanctions have devolved into mere moral suasion, devoid of any real enforcement power.

China has no need to circumvent sanctions. China simply seeks to normalize trade. Four lane bridge is, quite literally, infrastructure for such normalized commerce. It is not loophole. It is alternative path. As old bridge, China North Korea Friendship Bridge, built by Japanese in 1937, grew aged and limited in capacity, new bridge represents enhancement in efficiency. Under sanctions regime, such increase in efficiency carries inherent strategic significance: it allows scale of trade to surpass thresholds envisioned by architects of those sanctions.

TRUE WEIGHT OF THIS FLASH VISIT: BRIDGE REMAINS, TRUCKS WILL MOVE, TONNAGE REWRITES POLITICS

Kim Jong Un spent few hours in Dandong. He laid wreath. He toured factory. He crossed bridge, and then he crossed it back.

Yet bridge had been waiting there for twelve years before he ever set foot on it. It was not built for him. It was built for cargo. And flow of cargo has power to reshape nation economic structure and, by extension, political choices.

Beijing has not lifted sanctions against North Korea. Beijing has simply opened bridge that was already built. Bridge existence predates sanctions, and its opening comes after peak of those sanctions. This is transcendence of them, physical, irreversible act that re anchors North Korea economic future to this side of Yalu River.

Kim Jong Un may have crossed and returned, but bridge remains. Trucks upon it will continue to move, and with every truck, relationship between North Korea and outside world is being rewritten, through sheer tonnage.

🥚🛸 An egg-shaped object is strange enough. The next question is how it would move without obvious flight-control surfaces.

David Grusch, a former U.S. Air Force intelligence officer, discussed reports of egg-shaped craft during his conversation with podcast host Joe Rogan. He said he had heard about them from people dealing with such objects.

Grusch suggested that these eggs were usually unmanned and might be probes. That was a possible explanation, rather than a confirmed answer about what every reported egg-shaped object was doing.

The conversation then turned to the exterior. There were no obvious control surfaces in the account being discussed. Rogan asked whether the technology might be built into the skin of the object itself.

That idea was a question, not an established mechanism. A smooth shape does not tell us what is inside, what powers it, or whether anyone controls it remotely.

But it changes what people expect to see. Familiar aircraft give us visible clues about how they fly. A plain egg would offer far fewer clues from the outside.

If something could move without those familiar features, would you expect a probe or an entirely different kind of vehicle?

#UAP #UnusualCraft #Disclosure #frayingreality

‘Survivors are Not Your Audience’ by Julie Jewels Smoot is on #SoundCloud https://t.co/Mi2DctjYqc 

Survivors Are Not Your Audience is a fierce, unapologetic protest anthem confronting the repeated appearance of unwanted sexual imagery on social media, the disregard for personal boundaries, and the responsibility of digital platforms to respect the people who use them.

I wrote this song because I am tired of opening X and encountering pornography I never asked to see.

I am tired of being told to scroll past it.

I am tired of having my boundaries treated as an inconvenience.

And I am tired of a digital culture that too often measures engagement without considering the human beings behind the screens.

SURVIVORS ARE NOT YOUR AUDIENCE.

We are not simply clicks, impressions, statistics, or potential customers.

We are human beings.

We have histories.

We have boundaries.

And we have the right to decide what we want to see.

As a survivor of childhood sexual violence, I know that unexpected sexual imagery can bring painful memories and emotions to the surface. I was exposed to pornography when I was eleven years old and subsequently raped.

I was a child who deserved safety, dignity, and protection.

What happened to me was not my choice.

But today, as an adult woman, I am reclaiming my ability to make choices about my life, my environment, and my personal boundaries.

I refuse to accept that using a social media platform means surrendering those choices.

Through heavy industrial percussion, distorted electric guitars, haunting atmospheric textures, dramatic orchestral strings, and commanding female vocals, Survivors Are Not Your Audience transforms frustration into a powerful demand for accountability.

The verses explore the emotional impact of unwanted exposure and the exhaustion of repeatedly having to defend boundaries.

The chorus becomes a collective declaration:

SURVIVORS ARE NOT YOUR AUDIENCE!
WE ARE NOT YOUR CLICKS OR VIEWS!
WE ARE NOT YOUR TARGET MARKET!
WE HAVE EVERY RIGHT TO CHOOSE!
This song is not about denying consenting adults the freedom to make their own choices.
It is about recognizing that the freedom to share sexual content does not eliminate another person's right to avoid it.
It is about meaningful filtering options, effective content preferences, and platforms that take unwanted exposure seriously.

It is about demanding that a person's boundaries be respected without requiring them to disclose painful experiences to justify those boundaries.

Survivors should not have to explain their trauma before their choices are treated as valid.

We should not have to repeatedly encounter material we have tried to avoid.

And we should not be expected to surrender our peace simply because an algorithm prioritizes attention.

OUR BOUNDARIES ARE NOT YOUR GAME.

As Sound Alchemist Julie Jewels Smoot, a United States Navy veteran, author, independent musician, and survivor advocate, I create music that explores the full range of human emotion.

Some of my compositions offer stillness through gongs, Tibetan singing bowls, handpan, and meditative soundscapes.

Others give voice to grief, anger, injustice, and the determination to reclaim personal power.

Survivors Are Not Your Audience belongs to that second category.

It is loud because the message matters.

It is confrontational because silence has never been a requirement for dignity.

And it is deeply personal because I know what it means to have choices taken away.

I am not asking for pity.

I am asking for respect.

I am asking for meaningful digital boundaries.

I am asking social media platforms to recognize that their users are people, not just engagement metrics.

This song is dedicated to survivors who are tired of being dismissed, to people who want greater control over their online experiences, and to everyone who believes that consent and personal autonomy deserve recognition in digital spaces.

WE ARE HUMAN.
WE HAVE BOUNDARIES.
WE HAVE CHOICES.
WE HAVE VOICES.

I will continue sharing my music.

I will continue writing poetry.

I will continue speaking about survivor dignity and personal autonomy.
And I will continue refusing to apologize for the boundaries I establish.
SURVIVORS ARE NOT YOUR AUDIENCE.
OUR VOICES WILL BE HEARD.

Sound Alchemist Julie Jewels Smoot

text:
This is from Grok.

Yes, there is substantial documented evidence of this pattern of H1B fraud involving shell companies, staffing firms (“body shops”), and related schemes.
People who are already in the US (often on prior visas) or operators with ties to foreign workforces set up networks of U.S. LLCs or consulting/staffing companies. These entities then sponsor other foreign workers for H-1B visas, frequently using tactics like:
•Multiple lottery registrations via related shell companies to boost selection odds.
•Ghost offices or non-operating entities that claim active businesses and bona fide jobs that do not exist.
•Benching (not paying workers until/unless placed with a third-party client) and wage-related issues.
•False representations about specific end-client jobs in petitions.
Key Evidence and Examples
Bloomberg’s 2024 investigation, based on federal data obtained via FOIA, found that outsourcing and IT staffing firms received a large share of H-1B visas. It estimated that roughly one in six visas awarded in recent years (around 15,500 in one period) involved “multiple registration” gaming—submitting the same worker’s name through multiple companies to get extra lottery entries. Federal officials have described this as fraud. One documented operator, Kandi Srinivasa Reddy (who came to the US, earned a master’s degree, worked as a consultant, and founded Cloud Big Data Technologies LLC in 2013), controlled a network of about 13 related companies with overlapping addresses, management, and business models. These submitted thousands of registrations (e.g., over 3,000 for roughly 288 workers in one year) and secured hundreds of H-1Bs since 2020. Workers were often placed with clients (including major corporations) while the firms took a percentage of pay.
USCIS has treated coordinated multiple registrations by related entities as improper/fraudulent. It has issued notices of intent to deny or revoke, conducted investigations, and changed rules (around 2024) to limit the practice. Agency materials and decisions highlight indicators such as shared addresses, management, attorneys, IP addresses, and similar filings.
Prosecutions and investigations include:
•Department of Justice cases involving staffing firm owners who pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit visa fraud. Examples include filing petitions claiming specific jobs at end-client companies that did not exist, then marketing the approved workers elsewhere (e.g., Nanosemantics in San Jose; cases involving S-Team Software and related entities using false employment claims).
•Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton’s 2026 investigation into nearly 30 North Texas businesses for suspected H-1B abuse, including “ghost offices” that falsely represented active operations solely to sponsor foreign workers. Named entities include various IT/tech LLCs; demands sought employee records, financials, and operational details.
•Other documented patterns involving benching without required pay, false job descriptions, and wage kickbacks in staffing/consulting firms (noted in Economic Policy Institute reporting, DOL Inspector General probes, and indictments).
Large Indian-origin IT outsourcing and staffing firms have long been major H-1B users and have faced scrutiny for related practices (lottery flooding, placement models, wage issues). A significant share of the annual H-1B cap has gone to these categories rather than direct employment at product companies.
Context and Limits
Legitimate companies (including startups) can sponsor H-1B workers, and recent rule changes have clarified that founders with controlling interests can sometimes be sponsored by their own companies if there is a real job offer and specialty occupation. The fraud cases center on non-bona-fide offers, shell networks created primarily for visa gaming, and related misrepresentations.
Enforcement has included USCIS revocations, DOJ criminal cases, and state probes, though critics note

Arsenal return to Premier League action against Everton with confidence high after the midweek Champions League clash against Bayern Munich. But with Bukayo Saka sidelined through injury, Mikel Arteta needs others to take responsibility.

EZE — TIME TO TAKE CENTRE STAGE

Weekend Agriculture
Publishing Date: October 24, 2026

As late October sets in across the nation's midsection, the 2026 row crop harvest is barreling into its final stretch. The USDA's latest Crop Progress report confirmed that national corn harvest surged to 65% complete well ahead of the five year average of 52% while national soybean harvest reached 81% complete, beating the 67% historical norm. Ideal fall weather across the Corn Belt and Plains provided seamless combine momentum, allowing operators to make rapid headway as corn moisture levels drop naturally in the field.

Grain and livestock boards closed Friday's session with active positioning as traders weighed rapid harvest throughput against steady export movement and macro energy influences. CME corn and soybean futures experienced two way trade into the weekend, with November soybeans holding firm baseline support as processors maintain strong crush capacity. In livestock country, live cattle and feeder futures closed with solid gains, backed by tight market ready feedlot inventories and steady cash bids.

USDA AND POLICY DIGEST

The grain trade spent the week processing the latest USDA Crop Progress metrics alongside harvest logistics data, as combine activity approaches completion in several early districts:

National corn harvest reached 65% complete across major reporting states, with maturity virtually finalized at 98% nationwide. Harvest pace remains exceptionally swift across Iowa, Illinois, and Minnesota, with field reports confirming variable dryland yields alongside strong, consistent numbers on heavier, well drained soils.

Soybean harvest advanced to 81% complete nationally, with many Midwest districts entering final cleanup passes. Commercial processors and river terminals report heavy intake volumes, though firm domestic crush margins continue to support cash basis levels.

Evanston built a reparations blueprint. Now Washington is coming for the foundation.

Evanston, Illinois, did something most governments have spent generations avoiding: it moved reparations out of the speech and into the budget.

Now that blueprint is spreading across the country. And the Trump administration's Justice Department is challenging the rules that make it work.

VERIFIED FACTS

Former Evanston alderwoman Robin Rue Simmons helped turn the city's reparations promise into an actual government program. Now, through her organization FirstRepair, she's helping more than 100 communities explore how to do the same.

Evanston offers eligible Black residents and descendants up to $25,000 toward buying a home, paying down a mortgage or making repairs. The city committed $20 million and has already distributed more than $7 million, partly financed through local cannabis taxes.

But on October 16, the Justice Department entered an existing federal lawsuit against Evanston, arguing that its race- and ancestry-based eligibility rules violate the Constitution's Equal Protection Clause.

The government isn't simply criticizing reparations. It's asking a court to rule against the legal structure supporting Evanston's program.

And Evanston isn't the only institution wrestling with what repayment looks like.

Harvard dismissed a research team that had identified nearly 500 descendants of people enslaved by university leaders and donors. Georgetown continues offering educational support to descendants. Virginia Theological Seminary makes annual cash payments through a reparations endowment that reportedly grew from $1.7 million to $2.8 million.

Different institutions. Different obligations. Different ways of answering the same question: What does accountability look like when the people who profited are gone, but the institutions and advantages remain?

WHY IT MATTERS

For decades, reparations opponents could dismiss the idea as politically impossible or administratively unworkable.

Evanston complicated that argument.

It established funding, eligibility requirements, application records and a system for delivering benefits. It demonstrated that reparations could operate as public policy rather than remain an unresolved historical argument.

That's precisely what makes the legal challenge consequential.

The fight is no longer just about whether reparations are justified. It's about whether government can legally direct resources to the people a specific history of discrimination harmed.

If the federal challenge succeeds, cities considering similar programs may have to redesign their approach. Some could turn to geographically targeted programs, remedies tied to documented institutional harm, or private endowments. Others may abandon race-conscious eligibility altogether.

But those alternatives raise another problem: a program designed to help everyone isn't necessarily a program that repairs a specific injustice.

There's also a distinction worth watching. A city distributing public money faces different constitutional constraints from a private institution using its own endowment. A ruling against Evanston would not automatically outlaw every reparations initiative.

And that's where the next battle sits.

More than 100 communities are studying a model Evanston helped prove could operate. The federal government is testing whether its eligibility rules can survive constitutional scrutiny.

Evanston figured out how to move reparations from an argument to a payment. Now the courts may decide who government is allowed to repay.

Bijan Robinson — OVER 120 TOTAL YDS

Jonathan Taylor — UNDER 100 RUSHING YDS

Full Breakdowns Below.👇

1. BIJAN ROBINSON — OVER 120 TOTAL YDS
Robinson has rushed for 641 yards through six games, averaging 5.8 yards per carry, while adding 20 receptions for 144 yards. San Francisco allows just 90.2 rushing yards per game, ranking seventh in the NFL, making this a challenging matchup, but Bijan’s receiving ability gives him another path to 120 total yards.

2. KENNETH WALKER — UNDER 125 TOTAL YDS
Walker has topped 100 rushing yards in four of his five games, making this an aggressive under call. Seattle has allowed just 76.8 rushing yards per game to opposing running backs, giving Walker a difficult matchup against his former team and one of my boldest predictions to date.

3. JONATHAN TAYLOR — UNDER 100 RUSHING YDS
Taylor faces a Minnesota defense that could make Indianapolis work for its rushing production. If the Colts fall behind, the game script could shift toward more passing and reduce Taylor’s rushing opportunities, giving him limited opportunities to surpass the 100 yard mark in Week 7.

4. OLLIE GORDON — OVER 110 TOTAL YDS
Gordon is coming off consecutive productive performances, including 100 rushing yards against Minnesota and 88 against Cincinnati. He faces the Jets next, and if Miami gives him a workload similar to his recent games, he has a chance to reach 110 yards, but he’ll need more opportunities in the passing game to achieve this mark. Look for Miami to lean on him more coming off a bye week.

5. TYLER HIGBEE — TOP-10 TE
Higbee has shown he can earn a meaningful role, posting 83 receiving yards against Buffalo in Week 5 and playing 83% of the snaps in Week 6. With Davante Adams out, there may be room for more involvement in the Rams’ passing game and if WR Puka Nacua is limited or unable to play, Higbee’s role could increase more.

6. BO NIX — OVER 225 TOTAL YDS
Arizona has allowed an NFL-high 16 passing touchdowns, along with a 116.5 passer rating and 8.6 yards per attempt to opposing quarterbacks. QB Bo Nix has struggled to produce passing volume in recent weeks, so this prediction requires a bounce-back performance against a defense vulnerable through the air. If Payton truly trusts Nix, this would be very attainable given the matchup and opportunities the Broncos will have to exploit Arizona’s defense through the air.

7. JALEN COKER — OVER 65 RECEIVING YDS
Coker is currently the WR13 in fantasy points per game so far this season. His target rate for the year is 25.7%. Despite missing two games this year, Coker caught six passes for 97 yards on 13 targets in Week 6. Look for him to continue his momentum and exceed the over.

8. DANIEL JONES — OVER 200 TOTAL YDS
Daniel Jones returns to a familiar defensive system after spending part of a season in Minnesota in 2024, where Brian Flores and Jones know each other very well. His 5.9 yards per pass attempt against the blitz shows the challenge, but his stronger completion percentage and touchdown-to-interception ratio in those situations offer a stronger than usual path past 200 total yards.

This contribution need not wait until the war ends. Planning can begin now. Indeed, the sooner we begin preparing for peace, the better prepared we will be when the opportunity for national recovery emerges.

How can we learn from our past as we prepare for our future? The history of Sudan offers both inspiration and important lessons. The October Revolution of 1964, the uprising of 1985, and the December Revolution of 2018 demonstrated the extraordinary capacity of our people to mobilize peacefully in pursuit of freedom, dignity, and democratic governance.

Yet our repeated transitions have also revealed the fragility of democratic institutions and the difficulty of turning revolutionary aspirations into sustainable systems of governance. We must confront these lessons with honesty and humility. We must acknowledge the mistakes of past transitions, including our own. Political agreements are not enough unless they are supported by functioning institutions, broad social legitimacy, and mechanisms of accountability.

We must also move beyond the politics of exclusion and zero-sum competition. Sudan cannot be governed sustainably through the dominance of one region, one ideology, one political organization, or one faction. Our future depends on building a state that belongs equally to all its citizens.

This requires a fundamental shift in political culture: from confrontation to dialogue, from exclusion to inclusion, from militarization to civilian governance, from patronage to accountable institutions, and from the pursuit of power for its own sake to the understanding of political leadership as public service. These changes will not happen overnight. But without them, we risk reproducing the very conditions that brought Sudan to its present tragedy.

Let me turn to a message of hope.

Ladies and gentlemen, despite the devastation of the past three and a half years, I refuse to believe that Sudan’s future must be defined by war. Our people have demonstrated extraordinary courage and resilience. We have witnessed young volunteers risk their lives to deliver food and medicine. We have seen women organize relief networks and support displaced communities. We have seen professionals maintain essential services under the most difficult circumstances. And we have seen Sudanese communities around the world mobilize resources, expertise, and solidarity.⤵️

Adele Astaire (born Adele Marie Austerlitz; September 10, 1896 – January 25, 1981) was an American dancer and entertainer. She was Fred Astaire's elder sister, and his partner in a 27-year career in vaudeville and theater, beginning when he was five and she was eight. Fred Astaire (born Frederick Austerlitz; May 10, 1899) Omaha, Nebraska; died, June 22, 1987 (aged 88), Los Angeles, California

3) Fred and Adele in "Band Wagon," 1931, her final show before she married Lord Cavendish of England after 27 years dancing with Fred.
Adele was friends with Winston Churchill and played backgammon with him aboard the RMS Majestic on the way to England. When they arrived in port, reporters were there to photograph Adele, but Churchill distracted them and she slipped away.
When she was met her mother-in-law instead of a stately entrance into the room, she cartwheeled across the carpet.
Her wedding to Cavdendish was delayed when he came down with appendicitis.
She used her own money to upgrade Lismore Castle with modern plumbing.
She lost her first baby, who had been born pre-mature. A year later she carried twin boys who came into the world still born. Cavendish became an alcoholic and spent much time away from Adele at spas and hospitals fighting his addiction. 
David Selznick and other Hollywood heavyweights tried to lure Adele back into show business but she refused each offer. After another failed pregnancy, she joined the Red Cross and wrote 130 letters a week to American service men during WW2.
Cavendish died of alcoholism at 38 years of age after 12 years of marriage. The Cavendish family loved Adele and agreed she might continue to reside at Lismore Castle 3 months of each year which she did throughout her life.
Following a brief courtship, she married an old American comrade from her WWII days, Kingman Douglass. The couple had first met during World War II at the Rainbow Corner, a United Service Organizations club in London frequented by American servicemen, where Douglass, then serving in intelligence roles with the U.S. Army Air Forces, encountered Astaire, who was residing in England after her 1932 marriage to Lord Charles Cavendish.
During World War I, Douglass served as a captain and pilot with the 91st Aero Squadron, the "Demon Chasers," engaged in aerial observation and photographic intelligence. He was awarded the Distinguished Service Cross.
Douglass returned to military service in WW2 as a member of the Eighth Air Force flying combat missions. He served as the senior United States Army Air Corps intelligence liaison officer assigned to the British Air Ministry and in the Allied Intelligence Group in the Pacific Theater. After the war, Douglass established the new Central Intelligence Agency, serving as its deputy director for a few months before returning to finance. Later, he returned to intelligence as assistant director of the CIA, from 1950 through July 1952
Back in December, 1922, Douglass had married Helen Field James, the daughter of Howard James and Sophie Ayers. The couple had three sons: Abner Kingman Douglass, Howard James Douglass and William Angus Douglass. They were later divorced and Douglass married Adele Astaire in 1947.
Adele became step-mother to three lively boys and began to enjoy life with a vacation home in Jamaica, time at Lismore Castle and New York.
Douglass was severely injured when struck by a bus and then, not long after suffered further injuries in a car accident. In 1971 he died of a brain hemorrhage.

Lesson 46✝️- The Last Supper-Part 1

1. Everywhere Jesus traveled, He was followed by crowds of people. Some wanted Him to feed them or to heal their diseases. Others wanted Him to give them political freedom from the Romans. Not very many of them thought about their spiritual needs. Only a few realized that their greatest need was for Salvation from sin, Satan, and death. What do you want from Jesus? Think about that during this lesson.

2. Jesus and His disciples were traveling to Jerusalem. On the way, they came to the village of Bethany, where His friends Mary, Martha, and Lazarus lived. Not long before this, Jesus had raised Lazarus from the dead. Jesus sent two of His disciples ahead into the village. He told them they would find a young donkey tied up there, and they were to untie it and bring it back to Him. The disciples found the donkey and untied it. Some people asked them what they were doing. The disciples said, as Jesus had told them, that the Lord needed it, so the people let them take the donkey. (Mk. 11:1-6)

3. Jesus sat on the young donkey and rode into Jerusalem. (Mk. 11:7-10) Many people came and shouted praises to Him as He rode. They praised Him as the One Who came in the name of the Lord to bring back the kingdom of David. They covered the road with garments and with tree branches. This was foretold by the prophet Zechariah 500 years before it happened.(Zec. 9:9, Mt. 21:4-5)

4. Unfortunately, most of the cheering crowd did not believe that Jesus would save them from sin, from Satan’s power, and from God’s punishment. They just wanted Jesus to give them freedom from the cruel power of the Romans.

5. The Jewish leaders were afraid that the Romans would be angry about people following Jesus as a new king. They thought the Romans might bring an army to destroy Israel. The Jewish leaders lived a comfortable life in cooperation with the Romans, and they didn’t want to lose their position. They began to make plans to kill Jesus, but they were afraid of the people, who had seen Him do many miracles, and considered Him to be a great prophet of God. (Mk. 14:1-2)

6. The Jewish leaders tried to find a way to catch Jesus when He was away from the crowds. One of the disciples, Judas Iscariot, came to them and offered to help them find and capture Jesus if they would give him money. They happily promised to pay him if he would betray Jesus. (Mk. 14:10-11)

text:
At 3:27 on a January afternoon in 2009, Captain Chesley Sullenberger said one word: "birds." About 13 seconds later, with both engines losing power, he took the controls from his first officer, Jeff Skiles: "my aircraft." Sullenberger later told investigators that when he called for the engine failure checklist, Skiles already had it out.

US Airways Flight 1549 had left LaGuardia for Charlotte about two minutes before. The birds hit at 2,818 feet, about 4.5 miles from the airport. The checklist Skiles was working had been written for both engines failing above 20,000 feet.

So they split the job. Skiles worked the checklist. Sullenberger flew the plane, talked to the controller and picked where to land.

3:28 p.m. The controller offered a LaGuardia runway. "we're unable. we may end up in the Hudson." Offered another, he said, "I'm not sure we can make any runway," and asked about a small airport in New Jersey.

3:29 p.m. "we're gonna be in the Hudson."

3:30 p.m. The plane touched down on the river, about three and a half minutes after the birds.

He later told investigators a turn back to LaGuardia "would have been an irrevocable choice, eliminating all other options," and that the New Jersey airport "was too far away." The National Transportation Safety Board, the federal agency that investigates plane crashes, noted a return to LaGuardia meant crossing Manhattan.

In simulator runs, pilots who turned for an airport right after the strike landed in eight of 15 tries, but the board said those turns skipped the time needed to recognize the problem and decide. The one run that allowed a 35 second delay for that did not make it. The board found the river "provided the highest probability that the accident would be survivable."

All 155 people aboard lived. The board credited the crew's decisions and teamwork, the flight attendants' fast evacuation, boats and responders close by, and luck that this plane carried over water equipment it wasn't required to have.

One pilot kept the plane flying while the other worked the fix, and the hard option got said out loud about a minute in. When a plan breaks mid job, split it: one person keeps the work running, one works the problem. And say the hard option early, while there is still time to act on it.

text:
VIVEK RAMASWAMY’S $4 MILLION AD CALLS AMY ACTON A LIAR. BUT 1978 COURT RECORDS TELL A STORY THE AD LEAVES OUT.

TRUTH MATTERS NEWS | 2026 MIDTERM ELECTION REPORT
Updated: October 24, 2026

A mother appears in a political advertisement and tells voters that her own daughter is a liar.

The daughter is running for governor of Ohio.

The mother says she fabricated stories about her childhood.

And the Republican candidate who paid for the advertisement, Vivek Ramaswamy, is spending approximately $4 million to make sure voters see it.

But there is something the advertisement doesn’t explain.

The mother and daughter have been estranged for nearly 50 years following allegations of childhood sexual abuse—and court records document that the daughter’s stepfather was indicted for rape and fled prosecution.

Now President Donald Trump is defending the advertisement, Ohio’s Republican governor is condemning it, and election analysts are reassessing the race.

So what does the evidence actually establish?

WHAT THE AD SAYS

The advertisement features Donna Arthur, the biological mother of Democratic gubernatorial candidate Dr. Amy Acton.

Arthur accuses Acton of lying about her upbringing, including claims that she experienced homelessness and lived in a tent as a child.

She questions her daughter’s honesty and suitability for public office.

Ramaswamy’s campaign confirmed producing the advertisement and announced plans to spend approximately $4 million promoting it.

The campaign argues that voters should consider allegations about Acton’s truthfulness when evaluating her candidacy.

But the advertisement presents Arthur’s accusations without explaining the documented circumstances surrounding their estrangement.

That omission is central to the controversy.

WHAT THE 1978 COURT RECORDS SHOW

Acton has publicly described experiencing severe abuse during childhood, including sexual abuse by her stepfather, Cledith Arthur.

She says she and her brother were removed from their mother’s custody when she was 12.

Contemporaneous court records provide important corroboration.

In 1978, Cledith Arthur was charged and indicted for rape involving his 12-year-old stepdaughter.

He pleaded not guilty.

Court documents show that he subsequently failed to appear for proceedings, left his known address and became the subject of an arrest warrant.

He was never tried.

He later died.

An indictment is not a conviction, and the criminal allegations were never resolved at trial.

But the records independently establish that the criminal case existed and that the accused did not appear to face prosecution.

That is materially different from suggesting that Acton’s account of the legal proceedings was fabricated.

https://t.co/V39IUCbnBb, PolitiFact and other news organizations have examined the records and found corroboration for key elements of her childhood account.

WHAT ABOUT THE CLAIM THAT ACTON LIVED IN A TENT?

The advertisement specifically disputes Acton’s description of living in a tent during childhood.

But newly examined records contain references to Terrace Lake Park, a campground associated with the family’s history.

That supports the geographical context of Acton’s account.

It does not independently establish every detail of how long she lived there or the precise conditions of her housing.

Those distinctions matter.

The available evidence supports significant elements of Acton’s account. It does not prove every detail of her childhood memories.

Likewise, Arthur’s on-camera denial does not independently establish that her daughter’s account is false.

The relevant question is what documentary and corroborating evidence exists—not simply which family member makes the strongest accusation.

WHAT ACTON’S BROTHER SAYS

Acton’s brother, Philip Stearns, has publicly supported her account.

He describes a childhood marked by abuse and says his sister endured particularly severe treatment.

He has also criticized the campaign’s use of their estranged mother in the advertisement.

His statements provide additional family testimony.

But they should be distinguished from the independently documented criminal proceedings.

The court records establish the existence and course of the prosecution.

The siblings’ accounts describe their personal experiences.

Both are relevant, but they are different categories of evidence.

THE COMPETING POLITICAL PERSPECTIVES

RAMASWAMY’S ARGUMENT

Ramaswamy maintains that allegations about a candidate’s honesty are relevant to voters.

His campaign has argued that Arthur’s statements should be considered alongside Acton’s public descriptions of her upbringing.

President Trump has defended the advertisement, describing it as powerful and encouraging the campaign to continue airing it.

Vice President JD Vance has also defended the campaign against criticism.

Candidates routinely face scrutiny over their biographies and public claims.

That scrutiny is a legitimate part of elections.

But the reliability of a witness and the existence of contradictory documentary evidence are also relevant.

THE CRITICISM FROM WITHIN THE REPUBLICAN PARTY

Ohio Republican Gov. Mike DeWine has publicly called the advertisement wrong and urged Ramaswamy to withdraw it.

DeWine specifically referenced the underlying abuse allegations, the indictment and the history of estrangement.

Other Republican figures have also criticized the advertisement.

Importantly, DeWine has not withdrawn his endorsement of Ramaswamy.

That distinction demonstrates that criticism of this particular campaign tactic does not necessarily mean opposition to the candidate’s broader platform.

ACTON’S RESPONSE

Acton says she was removed from her mother’s custody following severe abuse and has not maintained a relationship with her for decades.

Her campaign argues that the advertisement exploits a traumatic childhood experience while omitting the records that help explain the estrangement.

That response is supported in significant part by the historical court documentation.

But the records do not independently resolve every disputed statement about her upbringing.

THE QUESTION OF FAIR CAMPAIGN SCRUTINY

Political candidates should expect their public claims to be examined.

Their records, policies, statements and representations to voters are legitimate subjects of reporting.

But evidence matters when personal accusations become campaign material.

A witness’s relationship to a candidate may explain why an allegation attracts attention.

It does not automatically establish credibility.

And a decades-long family estrangement may be important context when evaluating that witness’s account.

The relevant standard should apply regardless of party affiliation.

An allegation should be examined against the available evidence, whether it comes from a political opponent, a family member or the candidate themselves.

DID THE AD CHANGE THE OHIO GOVERNOR’S RACE?

The controversy has coincided with changes in prominent election forecasts.

On October 22, Sabato’s Crystal Ball moved its assessment of the Ohio governor’s race from Toss-Up to Lean Democratic.

On October 23, the Cook Political Report made the same change, citing the advertisement’s fallout as part of its assessment.

These are the judgments of outside election analysts—not election results.

They do not establish how individual voters have responded to the advertisement.

Nor do they prove that the controversy alone caused changes in voter preferences.

Some polling conducted before or during the controversy already showed Acton ahead, meaning the political environment cannot be attributed entirely to this one advertisement.

A forecast change is not proof that an election has been decided.

Ohio voters will make that determination on November 3.

WHAT WE STILL DON’T KNOW

How many voters have seen the advertisement?

How many believe Arthur’s accusations?

How many have examined the court records?

Will the controversy affect turnout or candidate preferences?

Are there additional records that could clarify disputed details of Acton’s childhood?

And how will voters weigh this controversy against the candidates’ competing proposals on Ohio’s economy, education, healthcare and state government?

Those questions remain open.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE CAMPAIGN

The controversy illustrates how a political advertisement can be authentic while still presenting an incomplete evidentiary picture.

Arthur really appears in the advertisement.

She really makes the accusations.

Ramaswamy’s campaign really produced and promoted it.

But authenticity alone does not establish the accuracy of the claims.

A real video can contain unsupported allegations.

A real witness can offer testimony that conflicts with historical documents.

And a political message can omit facts that materially affect how viewers understand it.

That is why verifying the source of an advertisement is only the beginning of evaluating its claims.

THE TRUTH MATTERS TAKEAWAY

Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign has produced a multimillion-dollar advertisement featuring Amy Acton’s estranged mother accusing her of lying about her childhood.

That is confirmed.

President Trump has defended the advertisement.

Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine and other Republicans have criticized it.

Those reactions are documented.

But historical court records also establish that Acton’s stepfather was indicted for rape in 1978, failed to appear for prosecution and was never tried.

The records, together with additional reporting and family testimony, corroborate significant elements of Acton’s description of her childhood.

They do not establish every detail of her personal history.

And Arthur’s accusations do not establish that those details were fabricated.

THE AD IS REAL. THE ACCUSATIONS ARE DOCUMENTED AS STATEMENTS. THE COURT RECORD PROVIDES CONTEXT THE AD DOES NOT.

The question for voters is not whether political candidates should face scrutiny.

They should.

The question is whether that scrutiny is grounded in the available evidence—and whether important facts have been omitted.

Because an informed decision requires more than hearing an accusation.

It requires understanding what the evidence actually shows.

THE EVIDENCE IS YOURS. THE VOTE IS YOURS.

Truth Matters News

Facts First. Analysis Second. Solutions Third.

text:
Autism Service Dogs, Safety and Calm for Tampa Bay Families
Saturday, Oct 24, 2026

For many Tampa Bay families raising a child with autism, one of the biggest fears is a child slipping away in a crowd or out an open door. A trained autism service dog can be part of a safety plan, alongside free tools that local sheriff's offices and the University of South Florida already offer.

Hillsborough County's service animal guide lists sensory signal or social signal dogs, also called autism service dogs, among the types of service animals, next to guide, hearing, seizure and psychiatric service dogs. Every dog in the county must be registered, but residents with service dogs can ask to have the tag fee waived by sending a waiver form and a current rabies certificate to the Pet Resource Center.

Under the ADA, a service animal is a dog individually trained to do work or perform tasks directly related to a person's disability. US Department of Justice guidance names "preventing a child with autism from wandering away" as one example. A dog that only comforts by being there does not qualify. In schools, the guidance adds, staff may need to give some help so a student can handle their service dog.

What does the work look like? 4 Paws for Ability trains dogs in tethering, so a child who tends to run stays connected to the family, and in scent tracking to find a child who does wander, plus behavior disruption tasks like a nuzzle or lying across a lap. In Southwest Florida, Topaz Assistance Dogs in Naples lists deep pressure, wandering prevention and tracking among its autism tasks and says its autism applications are open.

Wandering safety does not rest on a dog alone. Florida revived Project Leo on July 1, 2026, with $250,000 for the USF Center for Autism and Related Disabilities to buy personal search and rescue devices, handed out free through participating sheriff's offices to people at risk of wandering, first come, first served. CARD USF serves Pinellas, Pasco, Hillsborough, Sarasota, Polk and Manatee, and lists SafetyNet tracking through the Pinellas, Pasco and Hillsborough sheriff's offices. The Pinellas County Sheriff's Office also runs Take Me Home, a free, voluntary registry with photos and caregiver contacts so deputies can help a person who cannot speak or identify themselves.

Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

Sources: Hillsborough County service animal guide via @HillsboroughFL, US Department of Justice ADA service animal FAQ, 4 Paws for Ability, Topaz Assistance Dogs, Florida Senate HB 1405 summary, CARD USF safety resources, Pinellas County Sheriff's Office via @SheriffPinellas, photos via Wikimedia Commons by Zipster969, CC BY SA 4.0, and Shannon Coates, CC BY SA 3.0.

text:
Perplexity Pro:

Hekate report delivered
The full research profile is in the shared Markdown document, with a companion timeline chart covering fifteen dated attestations from Hesiod to the modern revival. Every claim carries an evidence tag ([Ancient], [Late antique], [Scholarly], [Modern], [Contested]) so historical record, tradition-specific belief, and modern synthesis stay separate.
What stands out
•Hesiod’s Hekate is benign and universal. The Theogony gives her a share of earth, sea and sky, but not the Underworld; the chthonic and sorcery associations grow later, with Euripides’ Medea (431 BCE) as the first clear “goddess of witches” text (Theoi, Theogony; OCD).[theoi +1]
•Her name may mean “by whose will.” Clay’s reading links Hekatē to Hesiod’s repeated hekēti, “by the will of,” framing her as the goddess through whom prayers are fulfilled.[duke]
•At Lagina she was a civic saviour, honoured by a Roman Senate decree in 81 BCE and served by a children’s choir and a Festival of the Key.[cambridge]
•Rare powers in Tier 3 include midwife of Zeus on the Lagina frieze, taming the winds at Titane, Eileithyia-like power over labour pains, Nature “suspended from her back,” the oracle about Christ, and a formless-fire epiphany in the Chaldean fragments (Harvard CSWR; Theoi, Cult).[theoi +1]
•Modern inventions flagged: the Crone role, Hekate’s Wheel, the frog, and the November 16, November 30 and August 13 festival dates are all post-antique; the monthly Deipnon is the only date-safe ancient observance, and even its timing (dark moon vs. Philochorus’ 16th) is contested (Covenant of Hekate; Patheos).[hekatecovenant +1]
The comparative section (labelled as modern synthesis) offers hooks for a Celtic-leaning practice, including the Nehalennia dog-and-keys parallel and threshold pairings with Hermes and Janus. A safety note covers aconite, the plant the ancients credited her with “discovering.”
Would you like the Colombian Spanish companion document produced now, or held until you have reviewed the English version?

🎮 GAMING NEWS ROUNDUP | Sat, Oct 24 🎮

EA's wildest pitch yet, a studio fighting for its life, and Xbox putting a meter on the cloud. Here's what's going on 👇

🏈 OPEN-WORLD FOOTBALL?!
@EASPORTS revealed Project Gridiron in a company memo. It's a "social-first" open-world American football game, separate from Madden and College Football, with a persistent hub where you hang out and customize your avatar. It landed alongside news of 400 job cuts, the BioWare shutdown, and a Fight Night revival. Fans are split between confused and furious. Some dream of NFL 2K5 on steroids, and others just want to know why this is the priority after layoffs. More details are "coming soon."

🗡️ ARKANE LYON ON THE CLOCK
The Dishonored and Deathloop studio has until Nov 13 to find a buyer under France's Florange Law, or Microsoft moves ahead with closing it. 217 jobs are at stake, and Marvel's Blade is reportedly near the end of production. @jasonschreier reports several options are being explored to save it. Fingers crossed. 🤞

☁️ XBOX CLOUD GOES PAY-BY-THE-HOUR
@XBOX Cloud Playtime packs are live for Insiders: 10 hours for $3.99, 25 for $7.99, and 50 for $11.99. You don't need Game Pass, and the hours never expire. The catch is that starting in November, Game Pass cloud play gets capped at 15, 10, or 5 hours a month depending on your tier. Great deal or the start of metered gaming? 👀

💼 MORE XBOX SHAKE-UPS
Helen Chiang, Xbox's first-ever COO and the former head of Minecraft, is leaving just three months into the job. Reports also say a @netflix deal for Xbox game adaptations fell apart when Netflix offered $500M and Xbox wanted $800M.

🐺 BIGBY'S BACK
@telltalegames' The Wolf Among Us Remastered launches digitally Oct 29, with upgraded visuals, better audio, and a new Noir Mode.

📅 NEXT WEEK IS STACKED
🌾 Oct 27: Village in the Shade from @NISAmerica, a cozy farming sim crossed with Japanese horror and getting strong early reviews
🎯 Oct 27: Hush, the 30th @VALORANT agent, joins the roster
⚔️ Oct 28: Phantom Blade Zero hits PS5 and PC digitally
👁️ Oct 30: @devolverdigital brings the survival horror RPG Look Outside to Switch, Switch 2, PS5, and PS4

🦎 CROC IS GETTING PHYSICAL
Physical Platinum Editions of Croc 1 and 2 are coming to Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox in spring 2027. Xbox got added after fans asked for it directly. Small but dedicated! 💚

😩 BG&E2 WATCH, YEAR 18
A report from French outlet Origami says @Ubisoft's Beyond Good & Evil 2 is still in pre-production and has pivoted to a solo-first, story-driven game. It now beats Duke Nukem Forever for the longest development of any major game.

text:
In 2013 Jason Eck was changing the oil on lawnmowers and golf carts.

He was a Division I offensive line coach. Western Illinois had fired the head coach, and rather than pay out what it owed the assistants, the school kept them on payroll and sent them to work other jobs on campus.

Eck got the golf course. Then they moved him to a cubicle at the public transit center in Macomb, Illinois.

Here is how he describes it.

"I got transferred to the guy who ran the bookstore and the campus bus system."

Saturday night his New Mexico team is 5 and 1 with the best scoring defense in the country.

He has five kids. Here is what he says about those years.

"We've been in bad debt, bad financial shape. I've got five kids so it was nuts."

The man who ran that bookstore and bus system, Jude Kiah, is the one who talked him out of quitting. Kiah asked him whether he really wanted to walk away from everything he had put in. Eck started hunting jobs instead.

By that July he was the offensive coordinator at Minnesota State.

He walked on at Wisconsin as an offensive lineman. He thought about law school and never took the test. After the Rose Bowl he asked to coach instead.

His own dad coached college basketball. Toledo fired Jay Eck in 1991, less than a week after a one point loss with an NCAA tournament bid on it.

Jason took job after job after that. His wife Kimberly found out he had lost the Ball State job while she was going into labor with their third son.

Then South Dakota State, where John Stiegelmeier told him he would make a really good head coach. Idaho hired him in December of 2021 and he went 26 and 13 there. New Mexico hired him two years ago.

Last season the Lobos won nine games, beat UCLA, made their first bowl since 2016 and sold out a home game for the first time since 2007. He was Mountain West coach of the year.

And one of his linebackers is his son.

Jaxton Eck came out of Brookings, South Dakota with offers from Sioux Falls and Northern State. Division II. He played for his dad at Idaho, and when his dad took the New Mexico job he had North Carolina State, Michigan State and Stanford asking for him.

He went to New Mexico. Last season he had 115 tackles and shared Mountain West defensive player of the year.

Father and son won conference awards in the same season.

Now the part that complicates it. One good year is not a program. New Mexico has been bad for most of the last fifty years, and the hard truth about coaches who win there is that somebody bigger calls.

But here is what Jason Eck says now.

He does not know whether he would ever have become a head coach if his son had not played football.

Thirteen years ago he was changing oil on a lawnmower.

What were you doing right before the job that changed everything for you?

His Head is in heaven, his inheritance is reserved in heaven (1 Peter 1:3–4), and his blessed hope concerns the return of the Lord Jesus Christ (Titus 2:13). That is why the Christian can live as a stranger and pilgrim upon the earth without becoming spiritually homeless. The unsaved man may possess a country, property, reputation, and an impressive collection of earthly possessions, but without Christ he remains separated from the everlasting life God offers. The saved man may have very little of this world’s wealth, but he belongs to the household of the King. The distinction is not between rich and poor, educated and uneducated, or Baptist and Methodist. The decisive distinction is whether a man is in Jesus Christ.

But the Holy Spirit does not stop with citizenship. Paul adds the beautiful expression “of the household of God.” A household involves something more intimate than a legal arrangement. It involves belonging, relationship, and family identity. John 1:12 declares that those who receive Christ are given power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on His name. Galatians 4:6 states, “And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.” Romans 8:15 speaks of the Spirit of adoption, while Romans 8:16 declares that the Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are the children of God. That is a far cry from the notion that religious institutions manufacture children of God by performing ceremonies over them. A preacher can pronounce a blessing, a denomination can record a name, and a congregation can vote somebody into membership, but none of those operations accomplishes the new birth. Jesus Christ told Nicodemus, “Ye must be born again” (John 3:7), not that he must join another religious organization, accumulate sufficient sacraments, or find a priest qualified to issue him a spiritual birth certificate. When a sinner trusts Christ, God gives him a relationship that religion cannot manufacture. The household consists of those who truly belong to God through the saving work of His Son. And once that family relationship has been established, the believer does not become spiritually orphaned every time he stumbles. His fellowship may suffer, his service may be judged, and his Father may chasten him according to Hebrews 12:5–11, but divine chastening is not evidence that his spiritual birth has been canceled. The living temple is composed of those who have become God’s children through Christ, not those who have managed to maintain a perfect religious performance.

Now return to the larger argument of Ephesians 2. How can Jews and Gentiles, once separated by the ordinances associated with the Mosaic economy, become members of the same spiritual household? The answer is not that God has abolished His promises to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David. The answer is the cross of Jesus Christ. Ephesians 2:14 declares, “For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” Verse 15 speaks of making “in himself of twain one new man,” and verse 16 identifies the means by which both are reconciled unto God: “by the cross.” Then verse 18 gives the resulting privilege: “For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.” There is the movement from alienation to reconciliation, from separation to access, and from strangers to household members. The wall that divided Jew and Gentile in the former arrangement no longer prevents their unity in Christ during the present dispensation. Yet spiritual unity in the Church does not erase Israel’s national identity or transfer every promise made to that nation into the hands of a Gentile religious establishment. text:
Formula 1: The Pinnacle of Global Motorsports

Formula 1 (F1) is widely regarded as the highest level of automobile racing in the world. Combining cutting-edge technology, elite athleticism, glamorous destinations, and fierce international competition, Formula 1 has evolved from a niche European racing series into a global sporting phenomenon followed by hundreds of millions of fans.

A Brief History of Formula 1

The FIA Formula One World Championship was officially established in 1950, with the inaugural World Championship race taking place at Silverstone in the United Kingdom. The sport grew rapidly during the 1950s and 1960s, with legendary drivers such as Juan Manuel Fangio becoming international superstars.

Over the decades, Formula 1 has witnessed extraordinary technological evolution:

Rear-engine race cars replaced front-engine designs in the 1960s.
Aerodynamics revolutionized performance in the 1970s.
Turbo engines dominated the 1980s.
Advanced electronics transformed the 1990s.
Hybrid power units arrived in 2014.
A completely new generation of cars and power units debuted for 2026.

Today, F1 races on five continents and is one of the most watched annual sporting championships worldwide.

The 2026 Formula 1 Season

The 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship features 23 Grand Prix events from March through December. The season began in Australia and concludes in Abu Dhabi.

How Many Races Remain in 2026?

As of October 24, 2026, there are 6 races remaining in the 2026 season:

United States Grand Prix (Austin)
Mexico City Grand Prix
São Paulo Grand Prix (Brazil)
Las Vegas Grand Prix
Qatar Grand Prix
Abu Dhabi Grand Prix

The season finale takes place on December 6, 2026 in Abu Dhabi.

Formula 1's Most Iconic Venues
Monaco Grand Prix

Perhaps the most famous race in the world.

Racing through the streets of Monte Carlo
Luxury yachts line the harbor
Considered motorsport's ultimate glamour event
Nearly impossible to overtake
Monza (Italy)

Known as "The Temple of Speed."

Historic home of Ferrari
One of the fastest circuits on earth
Passionate "Tifosi" fans create an unmatched atmosphere
Silverstone (United Kingdom)

The birthplace of the Formula 1 World Championship.

Hosted the first F1 World Championship race in 1950
Home race for many teams
Spa-Francorchamps (Belgium)

Considered by many drivers the greatest circuit ever built.

Features the legendary Eau Rouge and Raidillon corners
Combines speed, elevation changes, and variable weather
Suzuka (Japan)

A driver's favorite.

Technical layout
Figure-eight design
Demands absolute precision
The Most Difficult Circuits
Monaco

One mistake means hitting a wall.

Singapore
Extreme heat and humidity
Night racing
Physical demands often rival a marathon
Suzuka
Technical high-speed corners
Very little margin for error
Spa-Francorchamps
Challenging weather conditions
Rapid elevation changes
Extremely demanding on driver confidence
Formula 1's Fastest Circuits
Monza (Italy)

Monza remains Formula 1's most famous high-speed venue.

Average race speeds frequently exceed 150 mph
Top speeds approach 220 mph
Las Vegas Strip Circuit

One of the fastest modern street circuits.

Long straights
High-speed nighttime racing
Jeddah Corniche Circuit (Saudi Arabia)
Fastest street circuit in Formula 1
High-speed walls create constant risk
Silverstone
Features several of F1's quickest corners
Why Is Formula 1 So Popular?

F1's popularity has exploded in recent years due to several factors:

Global Reach

Events occur across Europe, Asia, North America, South America, and the Middle East.

Technology

Fans are fascinated by:

Aerodynamics
Hybrid powertrains
Data analytics
Advanced engineering
Superstar Drivers

Drivers become global celebrities.

National Pride

Fans often support:

Their country's driver
Local races
Historic manufacturers
Netflix and Social Media

The "Drive to Survive" series introduced millions of new fans to Formula 1.

Luxury Lifestyle

F1 combines:

Luxury travel
Fine dining
Exclusive parties
Premier hospitality

IndyCar racing is often closer.
F1 features more advanced technology and larger budgets.

NASCAR emphasizes close-quarters racing and entertainment.
F1 emphasizes engineering excellence and international prestige.
Formula 1 vs Endurance Racing
Endurance racing tests durability.
F1 focuses on outright speed over approximately two-hour events.

Formula 1 drivers are among the world's most highly conditioned athletes.

Implementation is pending, and launch timing will be announced separately.

An ATS, or alternative trading system, is an SEC-regulated venue that matches buyers and sellers of securities without being a stock exchange, and a registered broker-dealer has to run it. tZERO Securities is one, and a FINRA member. Temple, registered with FinCEN as a money services business, gets to offer securities trading without building its own broker-dealer, the release says.

Temple's side is the software, with an order book for tokenized NMS securities (exchange-listed stocks) and ETPs, settled on Canton with asset and cash moving together.

Renting the license was the quick part. The release doesn't name a stock or ETP to list, so the first named security will tell us more than this agreement.

If you hold $CC, a working securities market would add traffic, and Canton burns CC to pay for it, but that won't show up until launch. For a broker's compliance team, the regulated counterparty would be a FINRA member, a name its onboarding checks already handle.

The counter is that Temple's $1.6B of Canton volume and its largest-platform line are its own claims, and there's no date.

The license is signed and the shelf's still empty.

I hold $CC and $CNTN.

Which tokenized stock or ETP do you expect Temple to list first?

Bye-anca is a psychopath who needs to inflict torment so she can position herself as Fina’s one and only safe space. She creates the problem, exacerbates the suffering, and then presents herself as the solution. It’s a vicious cycle of psychological control. 

That rotten woman has created an environment where she is simultaneously the source of conflict and the source of validation and comfort. 

And Fina’s desire for approval from this woman, her psychological dependence on her, speaks volumes about the extent of the control Bye-anca has been exerting. She’s a damn nut job. Her entire blueprint is essentially: “I’ll keep you in survival mode,  make sure to aggravate your situation by continuously tormenting you, and present myself as your salvation while at it.” 

Which brings me to why Fina’s presence in Toledo is paramount to her healing. The closer she gets to the people who genuinely love her, the weaker Bye-anca’s influence becomes, until, hopefully, the whole illusion finally comes crashing down. 

Claudia’s innate kindness and integrity, Marta’s selfless and unwavering love, Digna’s maternal warmth: these women represent everything Bye-anca’s artificial world doesn’t. And they offer Fina what Bye-anca cannot: unwavering honesty, emotional security, and love without conditions or control. The difference is clear: they want Fina to feel loved and free, while Bye-anca’s world turns love into something possessive and self-serving.

Fina may not recognize it yet, but her safety net has always been in Toledo. It has been woven by the women who love her unconditionally, who want her to be happy, and who want to see her thrive for her own sake, not theirs.

But the seeds of self-doubt, hurt, resentment and self-sabotage were already there, buried beneath Fina’s pain and disappointment, waiting for the right conditions to take root. All Bye-anca had to do was provide the fertilizer, exploit the vulnerabilities and nurture those feelings until they became Fina’s entire frame of reference. Bye-anca didn’t need to invent a new reality; she simply needed to distort the one Fina already believed in.

The way out, as I see it, is not to replace one dependency with another, but to help Fina rediscover her own judgement, rebuild her self-trust and recognize the difference between someone who needs her vulnerable and someone who wants her free. 

That, to me, is what breaking Bye-anca’s hold should ultimately look like—alongside self-awareness and accountability.

Florence: Cradle of the Renaissance and the Glory of Brunelleschi's Duomo

Few cities in the world have influenced the course of civilization as profoundly as Florence, Italy. Nestled in the rolling hills of Tuscany along the Arno River, Florence is often called the Birthplace of the Renaissance, a city where art, science, architecture, literature, and humanist thought converged to transform Europe. While Florence is home to countless treasures, no monument better symbolizes its ambition, ingenuity, and cultural significance than Filippo Brunelleschi's magnificent Duomo, the cathedral dome that forever changed the history of architecture.

A Brief History of Florence

Florence traces its origins to a Roman settlement founded in 59 BC. During the Middle Ages, the city evolved into a powerful commercial and banking center. By the 13th and 14th centuries, Florence had become one of the wealthiest cities in Europe, fueled by its thriving wool and textile industries and the influence of banking families, most notably the Medici.

Unlike many European cities ruled by monarchs, Florence functioned largely as a republic governed by powerful guilds and merchant elites. Wealth generated from commerce allowed citizens and rulers alike to invest heavily in art, architecture, and education.

The city's prosperity attracted some of history's greatest minds, including:

Dante Alighieri, author of The Divine Comedy
Leonardo da Vinci
Michelangelo Buonarroti
Sandro Botticelli
Galileo Galilei
Niccolò Machiavelli

The concentration of artistic and intellectual talent transformed Florence into the epicenter of a cultural movement that became known as the Renaissance.

Florence and the Renaissance

The Renaissance, meaning "rebirth," emerged during the 14th and 15th centuries as Europeans rediscovered the art, literature, and philosophy of ancient Greece and Rome. Florence became the movement's beating heart.

Florentine artists pursued realism, perspective, and anatomical accuracy unlike anything seen since antiquity. Architects abandoned purely medieval forms and turned toward classical harmony and proportion. Scholars embraced humanism, emphasizing human achievement, education, and inquiry.

The Medici family became the Renaissance's greatest patrons, commissioning works from artists and architects whose creations still define Western civilization. Their support transformed Florence into an open-air museum of artistic achievement.

Standing above all these accomplishments literally and figuratively was the immense cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore and its revolutionary dome.

The Cathedral of Florence: Santa Maria del Fiore

The Florence Cathedral, officially known as Santa Maria del Fiore, was begun in 1296 under architect Arnolfo di Cambio.

The cathedral was designed to be the largest church in Christendom. However, its builders faced a nearly impossible challenge.

The central crossing of the church required a dome nearly 150 feet wide, larger than any constructed since ancient Rome. Medieval builders lacked both the engineering knowledge and the technology needed to complete such an enormous structure.

For decades, the cathedral stood unfinished. The massive octagonal opening remained exposed to the sky, and many believed the project could never be completed.

Then came Filippo Brunelleschi.

Filippo Brunelleschi: The Genius Behind the Dome

Born in Florence in 1377, Filippo Brunelleschi originally trained as a goldsmith. He later became fascinated by mathematics, mechanics, and ancient Roman architecture.

A trip to Rome dramatically changed his career. Studying ancient ruins, particularly the Pantheon, Brunelleschi sought to understand how Roman builders had achieved engineering feats that remained unmatched for centuries.

When Florence announced a competition in 1418 to solve the cathedral's dome problem, Brunelleschi submitted an audacious proposal.

His design challenged conventional wisdom.

Rather than building a traditional wooden support framework beneath the dome, which would have required forests of timber unavailable in Tuscany, Brunelleschi proposed constructing the dome without full centering.

Most experts considered the idea impossible.

Brunelleschi proved them wrong.

The Construction of the Duomo

Work began in 1420 and continued for sixteen years.

The finished dome remains one of humanity's greatest engineering achievements.

Brunelleschi developed several groundbreaking innovations:

Double-Shell Construction

Instead of a single massive structure, the dome consists of two shells:

An inner dome providing structural strength
An outer dome protecting the interior and creating its majestic appearance

This significantly reduced weight while maintaining stability.

Herringbone Brick Pattern

Brunelleschi devised an ingenious brick-laying method known as the herringbone pattern.

The arrangement prevented bricks from sliding outward during construction and allowed the structure to support itself as it rose higher.

Hidden Reinforcement

Stone and iron chains embedded within the masonry act much like modern tension rings, preventing the dome from spreading under its enormous weight.

Specialized Machinery

Brunelleschi invented revolutionary hoisting equipment capable of lifting massive stones and materials hundreds of feet into the air.

His machines were so advanced that some historians consider them precursors to modern construction technology.

Why the Duomo Changed the World

Completed in 1436, Brunelleschi's dome became the largest masonry dome ever built.

More importantly, it marked a turning point in architectural history.

For the first time since the fall of Rome, builders had created a monumental structure that rivaled the greatest achievements of antiquity. Brunelleschi demonstrated that mathematics, engineering, and classical knowledge could solve problems once considered impossible.

His work directly influenced architects across Europe.

Without Brunelleschi's breakthrough, many of the world's most famous domes might never have been realized, including:

St. Peter's Basilica in Rome
St. Paul's Cathedral in London
The United States Capitol in Washington, D.C.
Numerous Renaissance and Baroque churches throughout Europe

The dome became a symbol of human ingenuity and the Renaissance spirit itself.

The Accademia Gallery

No discussion of Florence is complete without mentioning the Galleria dell'Accademia, one of the city's most important museums.

Founded in 1784, the Accademia's primary purpose was to serve as a teaching institution for artists. Today it attracts millions of visitors annually.

Its greatest treasure is undoubtedly Michelangelo's David.

Standing over 17 feet tall, David is widely regarded as the finest marble sculpture ever created. The statue embodies Renaissance ideals: physical perfection, human potential, confidence, and intellectual strength.

Visitors approaching David through the museum's grand gallery often experience one of the most dramatic artistic encounters in the world.

While the Accademia celebrates the pinnacle of Renaissance sculpture, Brunelleschi's dome represents the pinnacle of Renaissance architecture. Together, the two masterpieces illustrate Florence's unique role as a city where artistic beauty and technical innovation advanced side by side.

Experiencing the Duomo Today

Even in a city filled with masterpieces, the Duomo dominates the skyline.

The red-tiled dome rises nearly 375 feet above Florence and remains visible from virtually every corner of the historic center.

Visitors can:

Climb the 463 steps to the top of the dome
Explore Brunelleschi's engineering up close
Admire Giorgio Vasari's vast interior frescoes
Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of Florence and the Tuscan countryside

From the summit, one gains a sense of the vision and determination required to create such a structure six centuries ago.

Brunelleschi's Enduring Legacy

Florence possesses many magnificent attractions: the Uffizi Gallery, Ponte Vecchio, Palazzo Vecchio, the Medici Chapels, and the Accademia among them. Yet Brunelleschi's Duomo remains the city's defining masterpiece.

It is more than a church dome. It is a monument to innovation, courage, and intellectual curiosity. It embodies the Renaissance belief that human ingenuity could overcome seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

For travelers, standing beneath the soaring vaults of Santa Maria del Fiore offers more than a glimpse into the past. It provides an encounter with one of history's greatest achievements, a structure that announced to the world that a new age had begun.

In many ways, the Renaissance started not with a painting or a sculpture, but with Brunelleschi looking up at an unfinished cathedral and daring to imagine what others believed could never be built. Today, his dome remains the unmistakable symbol of Florence, the city that changed the world.
